articles.title: 9 ways to save money and avoid debt this Black Friday
articles.summary: Having a plan ready can help you avoid debt during Black Friday shopping — especially if you're using a credit card.
articles.body:

As retailers roll out early deals throughout November, Black Friday can seem more like an entire season than a single shopping day. But despite the early discounts, many Americans are still waiting until Thanksgiving weekend to tackle their holiday shopping.

Nearly two-thirds (64%) of consumers say they're likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their holiday shopping, according to a 2026 National Retail Federation survey . But affordability is also top of mind: 56% of holiday shoppers say the state of the economy will affect their spending plans this year.

Completing your holiday shopping list doesn't have to leave your bank account empty come January, though. Have a financial plan ready to help you avoid overspending this year — especially if you're using a credit card.

Here are a few things to keep in mind to avoid debt and save money this Black Friday and beyond.

Decide on a budget to guide your spending before you head out this Black Friday. Maybe it's the total you've already set aside in savings throughout the year for holiday shopping or simply a portion of your normal budget.

You can also get specific by breaking up your overall budget into subcategories. Say you have $500 to spend on Black Friday deals. If your main goal is to cross off the majority of your gift list, maybe you'll allocate $400 of that to gifts while reserving $100 for any great savings you come across for yourself.

Take a look back at last year's spending to help you budget better this year, too. Review your old statements and receipts. Were you satisfied with the amount you spent, or are there items you wouldn't repurchase?

Online and in-store retailers alike may bombard you with limited-time offers and must-have new items, but making a game plan before you shop can help you avoid falling prey.

Many big-box retailers and plenty of smaller merchants release Black Friday or Cyber Monday deals in the weeks leading up to the big shopping days. Use these previews to find savings on the items you need and make your shopping list early. And don't forget to look for roundups online cataloging the year's best discounts.

Once you have your list, compare prices across a few retailers. Just because an item is on sale doesn't mean you're getting the lowest available price.

If you're unsure whether you'll be able to pay down your balance in full by the time your monthly payment is due, a card with a 0% APR introductory offer for new purchases could be worth considering. After you open your account, you'll have several months (typically between 12 and 18) to pay down your balance before interest kicks in.

Just remember: You'll still need to make at least your minimum payment each month and pay your purchases off in full by the time the intro period ends. Otherwise, you'll start to accrue interest on your remaining balance at the standard APR, just like any other credit card.

Here are a few top 0% APR offers available today:

4. Rethink nonessentials if you already have credit card debt

Most shoppers' email inboxes are flooded even more than usual with deals and discounts throughout the holiday shopping season. But for some people, this might be a time to reduce spending instead of splurging.

If you already have credit card debt, consider whether Black Friday shopping is a good idea this year. Instead, reward yourself by making an extra payment toward your balances.

Consider using a cash-only method for holiday shopping. Withdraw only the amount of cash you can spend on gifts and other purchases, and leave your credit cards at home. And if you haven't already developed a debt payoff plan, start getting ahead of the issue now.

5. Take advantage of credit card rewards

Credit card rewards can offer a big boost to your holiday shopping savings. Take a look at the rewards categories on the cards already in your wallet before you start shopping. If you're doing most of your Black Friday shopping online, for example, you may have a card that earns bonus cash back on online retail purchases. Or if you're shopping at several different types of retailers, a card with a flat rewards rate on all purchases could make more sense.

Say you spend $500 on holiday gifts using a credit card that earns 2% cash back on all purchases. That's $10 in cash back on purchases you were already planning to make.

Just make sure you can pay off your balance in full by your payment due date. The interest you could accrue by carrying a balance can quickly outweigh the value of any rewards you earn.

Before you shop, look beyond sale prices for other opportunities to score deals. If you're shopping online, consider using browser extensions that can scour the internet for coupons and cash-back offers you may qualify for. In-store, some Black Friday retailers may price match discounts from other stores, helping you save the difference at checkout. Check the retailer's policy first, since some exclude Black Friday deals from price matching.

Start watching prices early and set up price alert notifications for items you want. Knowing what regular prices are in the weeks leading up to a big sale can help you decide whether the discounted price is actually worth it later.

Many credit cards provide benefits that can protect eligible purchases in case of accidental damage or theft. In some cases, you might also be able to receive reimbursement if a merchant won't accept an item for return. These perks could be especially useful if you plan on purchasing expensive holiday gifts, such as a new phone or television.

Here are some protection benefits to look out for when considering different types of credit cards (specific benefits can vary by card and card issuer):

Purchase protection: Covers eligible new purchases against damage or theft.

Extended warranty coverage: Provides additional warranty coverage to eligible purchases with existing manufacturer's warranties.

Cell phone protection: Covers eligible cell phones (on plans paid for by your applicable card) against damage or theft.

Return protection: Provides reimbursement for eligible new purchases if the retailer won't allow you to return them.

Check your card's benefits guide before you shop. These protections typically have coverage limits, exclusions, and other requirements.

Put your extra spending during the holidays to good use by earning a credit card welcome bonus on purchases you're already making.

Many credit cards require you to meet a spending threshold over the first few months to qualify for a sign-up bonus, so this could be a good time to align your increased spending with earning extra cash back, points, or miles.

Before you apply, make sure you can meet the spending requirement with purchases you've already budgeted for. Spending more than you planned just to earn a welcome bonus can cost you more than the bonus is worth.

It's common for credit card issuers like American Express, Chase, and Citi to provide targeted shopping offers to cardholders. These offers can help you save money if you make an eligible purchase from a specified retailer, and your targeted offers can vary.

For example, you might see an offer in your online account for 10% back on a Holiday Inn stay or 5% cash back on Sony electronics. These offers may not add a ton to your overall budget, but they can add up if you receive offers for purchases you were going to make anyway.

To use an offer, add it to your account, then make the eligible purchase with that credit card. There's often a limit on how much you can save, so be sure to read the offer details carefully.

articles.title: 66-year-old outdoors and Christmas retailer closing all stores
articles.summary: The American Sale liquidation has already begun, and anyone can take advantage online.
articles.body:
American Sale has never been a traditional retailer. The 66-year-old chain sells patio furniture, pools, hot tubs, game room supplies (like pool tables and dartboards), and a massive selection of Christmas merchandise.

It's a company based in Chicago, a part of the country that's not known for having a long pool season. It has managed to thrive for decades, partly by becoming a huge source of Christmas decorations to make it through the winter months.

That's an impressive run, but it's coming to an end.

American Sale will close all of its stores in early 2027. Liquidation sales are already underway and are taking place in all of the chain's locations as well as on its website .

American Sale was put up for sale, and a deal appeared to be made.

"After 66 years of proudly operating as a family-owned business, the Jones family is currently in the process of finalizing a sale with new ownership for American Sale," the company shared in a press release .

"This is an important moment in the history of American Sale," said the Jones family. "After 66 years, we are incredibly thankful for everyone who has supported our family and our business."

The company says most locations are expected to remain open through the rest of 2026, though stores may close gradually and customers should check the store locator for current hours. All sales are final, and merchandise cannot be held for delivery in 2027. Manufacturer product warranties remain in effect, while pool installation warranty questions should go to the installer. American Sale will honor gift cards and merchandise credits through Dec. 13, 2026, and has stopped selling gift cards.

The spa service center remains open and is scheduling service calls by request. Customers can text (708) 550-7665 for swim spa or hot tub service.

That sale has fallen through, as the company has issued a new press release detailing the shutdown.

"Earlier this year, the company had announced a sale of the business to a new owner. However, it has now been released that the transaction is no longer attainable, and the company will proceed to conclude operations sometime in early 2027," the company shared .

Tiger Group is running a going-out-of-business sale

American Sale has hired Tiger Group and Hyper Group to conduct what it's calling a Total Liquidation Sale.

articles.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
articles.summary: The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company's recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.

The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.

The petition states that its signers are "concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process" and demands that the board "bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts." It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public.

"Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice," the petition says.

Huang resigned on Thursday , four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs .

Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company's interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia's stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang's departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding .

articles.title: Prejuízo dos Correios atinge R$ 7,5 bilhões no terceiro trimestre | G1
articles.standfirst: Rombo da estatal aumentou em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, quando registrou prejuízo de R$ 5,9 bilhões; empresa está em reestruturação
articles.summary: Prejuízo dos Correios chega a R$ 7,5 bilhões no 3º trimestre, o 16º déficit seguido da estatal que agora aposta em plano de reestruturação e novos empréstimos.
articles.body:
Ponto de Coleta dos Correios em Belém — Foto: Divulgação

Os Correios tiveram prejuízo de R$ 7,5 bilhões até o terceiro trimestre de 2026, segundo o balanço contábil da estatal. O resultado representa um crescimento do rombo registrado no segundo trimestre, quando a estatal já teve um prejuízo de R$ 5,6 bilhões.

Com isso, os Correios completam o 16º trimestre seguido com déficit nas contas . Na comparação com 2025, quando o rombo foi de R$ 5,9 bilhões, o prejuízo também aumentou. Apesar disso, a empresa afirma que o resultado veio R$ 272 milhões melhor do que o esperado.

"Os indicadores de receitas e despesas mostram que os resultados seguem em linha com o planejamento para 2026", diz a estatal em nota. Os Correios atualmente têm um plano de reestruturação para tentar recuperar suas contas.

Segundo a estatal, o prejuízo é resultado de "pressões relevantes" enfrentadas pelos Correios nos últimos anos. Entre elas, redução de receitas vindas dos serviços postais tradicionais, elevação dos custos operacionais e necessidade da estatal manter sua estrutura capilarizada, ou seja, presente em todo o país.

O demonstrativo financeiro mostra ainda que a receita total da empresa no terceiro trimestre chegou a R$ 13,2 bilhões. Já as despesas somaram R$ 20,7 bilhões, cerca de 1,2% abaixo do planejado.

A maior parte da receita dos Correios teve como origem serviços e vendas oferecidos pela empresa. Foram R$ 11,7 bilhões recebidos dessa forma. Ainda assim, houve queda de 5,33% na comparação com os resultados do mesmo período de 2025.

Com ações até 2027, o plano de reestruturação dos Correios busca reorganizar a empresa para diminuir custos e modernizar seu modelo de negócios. Segundo a estatal, os resultados dessas ações têm "diferentes prazos" e devem ser observados somente no futuro.

"O monitoramento do Plano de Reestruturação evidencia a evolução da implementação das iniciativas destinadas ao aumento da eficiência operacional, à recuperação da competitividade e ao fortalecimento da capacidade de geração de receitas", diz o relatório contábil.

Ainda segundo o documento, uma das prioridades dos Correios no momento é manter a liquidez da empresa enquanto o plano é colocado em prática. Para isso, em outubro deste ano — depois dos resultados do terceiro trimestre —, a estatal conseguiu a autorização formal para o empréstimo de R$ 7 bilhões, anunciado ainda nos resultados do segundo semestre .

O empréstimo conta com garantia do governo federal. Com sua concretização, os Correios chegaram a R$ 19 bilhões em empréstimos desde o fim de 2025. A nova quantia bilionária tinha previsão de entrar no caixa da estatal somente no início de novembro, segundo o relatório contábil.

"A contratação representa avanço relevante na execução da estratégia de financiamento da Empresa, contribuindo para o fortalecimento das perspectivas de liquidez e para a sustentação financeira das operações durante o período de implementação das medidas de reestruturação", diz o documento.

articles.title: Tata Steel eyes NINL merger this fiscal; Rs 40,000 crore expansion awaits clearance
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel expects to bring Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) under its fold through a merger within the current financial year, with the final
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel expects to bring Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) under its fold through a merger within the current financial year, with the final approval from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) now awaited."The amalgamation of NINL with Tata Steel remains on track for completion this financial year," Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Tata Steel, said.The NCLT is scheduled to hear the matter later this month. Its final approval will pave the way for Tata Steel's proposed Rs 40,000 crore expansion at the NINL facility.Tata Steel acquired NINL's assets for Rs 12,100 crore through its erstwhile subsidiary, Tata Steel Long Products (TSLP). The acquisition was completed in July 2022 and included a steel manufacturing unit with an annual production capacity of 1 million tonnes per annum (MTPA).The company plans to add around 5 million tonnes of capacity to the facility, which is located about 5-10 km from its Kalinganagar steel plant. The proposed investment is part of Tata Steel's long products expansion plans in the region."We have... announced another 5 million tonne expansion in Neelachal (Ispat Nigam), which is also in Kalinganagar. It is a long products expansion, and we have announced that it is a Rs 40,000 crore project," Tata Steel CEO and Managing Director T V Narendran recently told PTI.NINL was the first state-owned steel company to be privatised by the Centre. articles.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang exited company in 2025, stays silent on 'personal matters'
articles.summary: Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has confirmed that Alice Huang, the former executive at the centre of the controversy involving Nvidia's Jensen Huang, left
articles.body: Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has confirmed that Alice Huang, the former executive at the centre of the controversy involving Nvidia's Jensen Huang, left the company in August 2025.The company told CNBC on Sunday that Alice Huang officially departed on August 30, 2025, and no longer holds any role there. It declined to comment on her personal affairs.“Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters,” the company said in an emailed statement.The announcement comes amid heightened scrutiny of Megaspeed following reports about Alice Huang's alleged relationship with Jensen Huang and her business connections in China. The New York Times has reported that US intelligence officials believe she was recruited by China's intelligence services to gather information on the Nvidia chief.Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife amid the reports and resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12. The reports also raised questions about another alleged relationship involving a senior Nvidia employee.Who is Alice Huang?Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, built a career in Chinese finance before moving into the artificial intelligence and cloud computing sector.She reportedly worked in television journalism before taking up roles in banking and investment management, including at HSBC's private banking arm in Hong Kong and Chinese investment bank CITIC Securities.She later held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm, where she was identified in company records as a deputy general manager and executive director. She became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed in March 2023, according to corporate records reviewed by research group C4ADS.Her business interests have also drawn attention because of reported links to Huawei. An investigation by private intelligence firm Tesari, shared with CNBC, found that Shanghai Hexi acquired a 27% stake in data centre developer Shanghai Century Longteng in 2021. Century Longteng held a controlling stake in Shenzhen Yifeng Technology, whose key customer was Huawei Cloud. Hexi exited its investment in Century Longteng in 2024.The findings establish an indirect business connection to infrastructure serving Huawei, but do not establish that the facility acquired Nvidia chips or that Alice Huang was involved in any unauthorised transfer of technology.Megaspeed under scrutiny over Nvidia chipsMegaspeed describes itself as a core regional business partner of Nvidia's cloud computing business. It allows customers to rent computing capacity powered by Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs), specialised chips used for complex computing tasks.The company, which operates in Singapore and Indonesia, has previously faced media and government scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia chips supplied through its business may have been redirected to customers in China.Megaspeed rejected allegations concerning its business, supply chain and global operations, saying the media reports were not supported by verifiable evidence. It said it had appointed external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation.The company added that its operational and supply-chain controls were designed to comply with applicable laws, including US export control requirements and regulations in the markets where it operates.It said it would review the reports and communicate further with stakeholders as appropriate.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Sebi plans AI guardrails for capital markets, stresses human oversight in critical decisions
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the
articles.body: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the capital markets, with a focus on investor protection, accountability and human oversight, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Sunday.The proposed guidelines will lay down safeguards for AI applications used by market participants, including disclosure requirements and accountability of regulated entities. A 'human-in-the-loop' approach will also ensure that critical decisions involving AI remain subject to human oversight, Pandey said, according to PTI.The regulator had floated a consultation paper in June 2025 proposing guiding principles for the responsible use of AI and machine learning in the securities market. The proposed framework aims to harness the benefits of the technology while addressing risks to investor protection, market integrity and financial stability.Pandey was speaking at the inauguration of Sebi's pavilion, titled 'Bharat Ka Share Bazaar', at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The pavilion, inaugurated on November 14, has been set up in association with market institutions, including the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Central Depository Services (India) Ltd (CDSL), National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) and the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI).The pavilion features an AI zone and an Investor Facilitation Camp, where visitors can interact with officials and learn about safe investment practices. It also aims to educate people about fraudulent investment schemes, unregistered entities and illegal mobilisation of funds.Pandey urged participating institutions to use their interactions with visitors to identify processes that could be simplified and services that could be improved. He also highlighted Sebi's 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' campaign under Project Jagrook and reiterated the message 'Check, Validate and Verify', asking investors to understand an investment, verify its authenticity and assess its risks before committing money.The regulator has also been strengthening its cybersecurity framework amid rising threats to financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, as well as digital frauds involving social media influencers. Sebi introduced a structured incident response mechanism in May, aligned with the Financial Stability Board's FIRE reporting template, Pandey said, reported ANI.On risks linked to quantum computing, the Sebi chief said the regulator was taking stock of cryptographic systems and identifying areas where the technology is used to assess potential vulnerabilities. Such risks could become more pronounced around 2032-35, making it important for markets to prepare in advance.Sebi has also developed supervisory tools, including 'Sudarshan', which is being showcased at international regulatory forums, and is working to strengthen its AI capabilities through global initiatives and supervisory toolkits.Sebi reviews listing framework for startupsPandey also said Sebi has set up a working group to examine ways to make the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) more attractive to startups, particularly deep-tech and biotech firms that may take longer to become profitable.The existing platform has not gained the desired traction, and the regulator is considering changes that could help such companies access public markets at an earlier stage. The aim is to give investors a clearer understanding of the higher risks involved while allowing them to participate in the companies' long-term growth potential.The 45th IITF, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, is being held at Bharat Mandapam from November 14 to 27. This year's theme is 'Vikas aur Virasat'.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Manipal Hospitals Q2 revenue grows 37.3%; net profit rises 21.6%
articles.summary: Manipal Hospitals Q2 revenue rose 37.3% to Rs 3,399 crore; net profit ex-exceptionals up 21.6% to Rs 380 crore, with margins declining.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Manipal Health Enterprises, which operates Manipal Hospitals, reported a 37.3% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 3,399 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 2,475 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.Net profit, excluding exceptional items, rose 21.6% to Rs 380 crore from Rs 313 crore. However, the net profit margin contracted by 140 basis points to 11.2% from 12.6% a year earlier. Reported net profit, including exceptional items, stood at Rs 285 crore, against Rs 318 crore in Q2 FY26.EBITDA increased 29.8% to Rs 882 crore, compared with Rs 680 crore in the year-ago quarter. EBITDA margin, however, declined to 26% from 27.5%, a contraction of 150 basis points. The company attributed its performance to sustained patient demand, growth in high-acuity specialties and improved capacity utilisation across its network.The current quarter’s results include Sahyadri Hospitals, which Manipal acquired in October last year, while the corresponding year-ago period does not include that acquisition. Sahyadri contributed Rs 375 crore in revenue and Rs 73 crore in EBITDA during the quarter.Commenting on the performance, Dilip Jose, managing director and CEO of Manipal Hospitals, said growth was driven by higher patient volumes, with more people accessing its healthcare services. Improved capacity utilisation, particularly in high-acuity specialties, was another key contributor.He said the company would continue to focus on strengthening clinical capabilities, improving operational performance and building a more integrated healthcare platform.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Italy fines Meta $887M over sly access into Android users’ photo galleries
articles.summary: Italy claims Meta has violated European privacy laws, giving them a timeline to disable the feature.
articles.body:
Italy announced an €805 million ($887 million) fine against Meta on Saturday for using photos and videos from Android users' galleries on Facebook without specific consent or adequate disclosure.

The Italian Data Protection Authority said the feature, called "Get suggestions from gallery when browsing Facebook," violated a European privacy directive incorporated into Italian law. The directive protects smartphones as part of a person's private sphere and requires "free and informed consent" for such access, the authority said.

Investigators found that the feature was enabled by default and that Facebook requested gallery access through a single permission covering multiple app functions with different purposes.

The authority gave Meta 60 days to disable the feature and seek separate consent for its use. Italy has about 20 million Android users, the agency said.

The fine was imposed on Meta Platforms Ireland Limited, which challenged Italy's jurisdiction, according to the statement.

The authority said Meta's "lack of cooperation" with the investigation factored into the penalty, which amounts to approximately 0.47% of the group's global turnover.

articles.title: SpaceX Catches Starship From Orbit for the First Time. Here’s What It Means for Starlink’s Costs
articles.summary: Key TakeawaysSpaceX caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time on Nov. 14, though it lost the Super Heavy booster on the same flig...
articles.body:
SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time on Nov. 14, though it lost the Super Heavy booster on the same flight.

Starship spending is weighing on the Space segment, which posted a $7 million operating loss in the third quarter, against $259 million in operating income a year earlier.

Most of the payoff from reusable ships would go to Starlink. Connectivity earned $2.37 billion in operating income last quarter, and 75% of the mass SpaceX put in orbit was its own payloads.

The stock closed Friday at $139.11, about 3% above its $135 IPO price. A caught ship flying again quickly matters more to the stock than the first catch itself.

SpaceX ( SPCX:NASDAQ ) caught a Starship upper stage with its launch tower for the first time on Saturday, Nov. 14, about 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase. Ship 42 flew 14 orbits and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the tower's arms closed around it, CNBC reported . "Mechazilla has caught the Starship," SpaceX's Dan Huot said on the company's livestream, Universe Today reported.

The flight wasn't clean. The Super Heavy booster's catch was called off minutes after liftoff on Friday, Nov. 13, when its onboard systems flagged a fuel-system problem, and it exploded before reaching the Gulf of Mexico. The catch also raises the bar for Rocket Lab ( RKLB:NASDAQ ), whose reusable Neutron rocket hasn't flown: Rocket Lab signed eight Neutron missions worth more than $515 million last quarter, but its first launch has slipped into 2027.

The case for the catch is cost. Starship carries far more than Falcon 9: Flight 14's 26 V3 satellites added about 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch, according to SpaceX's third-quarter results . SpaceX is also its own biggest customer. Of the 476 metric tons it put in orbit in the third quarter, 358 tons, or 75%, were its own payloads, mostly Starlink satellites. A ship that comes back to the tower instead of burning up is what turns that capacity into cheaper launches.

Starship Spending Weighs on SpaceX's Space Segment

Right now, Starship is a cost. SpaceX's revenue reached $14.58 billion in the third quarter, almost double the second quarter's $7.81 billion, but the Space segment contributed little of that growth.

The Space segment brought in $1.77 billion and lost $7 million, against a $259 million profit a year earlier. SpaceX said faster Starship R&D drove a $367 million rise in the segment's costs, and it spent $1.61 billion on Space capex, about 91% of the segment's revenue. Starlink is where the payoff should land: Connectivity earned $2.37 billion in operating income on $5.25 billion of revenue, a 45% margin, before any savings from reusable ships.

articles.title: Indian Railways has built freight corridors, but can it win back cargo from road transport & highways?
articles.summary: By Jagannarayan Padmanabhan Indian Railways is entering a new phase in freight transportation.
articles.body: By Jagannarayan PadmanabhanIndian Railways is entering a new phase in freight transportation.The eastern and western dedicated freight corridors (DFCs) are now fully operational, unlocking capacity and enabling faster, more reliable freight movement. More capacity is on the horizon, with a proposed east-west corridor set to strengthen connectivity across the country.After decades of investment constraints, rail freight finally has the infrastructure to compete. But infrastructure alone will not win back traffic from roads.The challenge is no longer building tracks. It is persuading customers to choose rail over trucks.At first glance, rail freight appears to be thriving. Freight loading has risen from 1,098 million tonne in fiscal 2015 to 1,617 million tonne in fiscal 2025 and a record 1,670 million tonne last fiscal. Yet rail's position within India's logistics system remains weaker than these numbers imply.A parliamentary committee recently estimated rail's share of national freight tonnage at only about 27% in fiscal 2025, well below the National Rail Plan's goal of 45% by 2030.The issue is not a shortage of freight. India's economy generates more than enough cargo to support that ambition. The problem is that roads are increasingly serving customers better.The competitive pressure is visible even in commodities that have traditionally been rail strongholds. Coal, iron ore, steel and cement remain the backbone of railway freight earnings, with coal alone contributing nearly half of freight revenue. Yet roads have steadily expanded their presence across several of these segments.Coal offers the clearest example. Road's share of raw-coal dispatches increased from 24.4% in fiscal 2021 to 33.8% in fiscal 2024 before easing slightly to 31.1% in fiscal 2025.Over the same period, rail's share fell from 53.9% to 47.4% before recovering to 50.5%. Rail may have regained some ground, but roads are now firmly established even in one of its most important freight categories.A similar story emerges elsewhere. Railways moved about 178 million tonne of iron ore in fiscal 2025 against production of roughly 289 million tonne, implying a rail transportation coefficient of just over 60%. Comparable ratios were materially lower for steel and cement. While these figures do not directly measure modal share, they underscore a broader point: a substantial portion of India's bulk freight still moves outside the rail network.The reasons extend far beyond pricing.India's freight geography is changing. Urbanisation, rising incomes and e-commerce are shifting consumption away from a handful of metropolitan centres towards hundreds of Tier II and III cities. India's urban population is estimated to have reached 522 million in 2025 and is projected to approach 600 million by 2036.More revealing is where demand growth is occurring. Tier II and III cities are estimated to have generated around two-thirds of incremental direct-to-consumer orders last fiscal. Warehousing, distribution and industrial activity are following the same trajectory, creating a logistics network that is increasingly dispersed.Road transport has adapted quickly to this reality. Supported by a national highway network that has expanded nearly 60%, from 91,287 km in 2014 to 146,204 km by March 2025, trucks can reach new warehouses, distributors, factories and construction sites directly. They offer flexibility, minimal handling and a single point of accountability from origin to destination.Rail, by contrast, remains primarily a line-haul business.Its challenge is not its dependence on trucks for first-mile and last-mile connectivity. Every major freight system relies on multimodal logistics. The problem is that the transition between rail and road often remains fragmented, creating additional handling, delays and uncertainty for customers.A cement producer or steel manufacturer does not evaluate only the railway tariff. It evaluates the cost, speed and reliability of the entire journey. A lower rail rate becomes irrelevant if cargo must be handled multiple times, delivery windows are uncertain or information is unavailable. Customers buy logistics outcomes, not transport modes.That is why the next frontier for Indian Railways is service quality.The DFCs will improve transit times, but faster line-haul movement is only part of the solution. Customers also need assured wagon availability, predictable departures, reliable arrival schedules and real-time shipment visibility. A steel plant cannot afford disruptions in raw-material supplies because wagons are delayed. An exporter cannot risk missing a vessel because cargo reaches the port late.Railways should therefore measure success not only through loading volumes and freight revenue but also through customer-centric metrics such as on-time arrivals, terminal turnaround times, schedule adherence and customer retention.Reliability must become a product.The same customer-first approach should guide the next phase of cargo-terminal development.The Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal programme has already expanded freight-handling capacity. The next step is to transform these facilities into integrated logistics hubs where cargo can be consolidated, stored, containerised and transferred seamlessly between rail and road.Success will depend less on the number of terminals built and more on where they are located and how effectively they connect with surrounding logistics networks. Facilities should emerge where manufacturing, warehousing and consumption are growing, not simply where railway land is available.Partnerships will be equally important. Railways need not extend tracks to every customer. Instead, it should work more closely with trucking companies, warehouse operators and third-party logistics providers to create integrated door-to-door solutions. Digital platforms offering unified booking, tracking and shipment visibility across modes can further simplify the customer experience.The objective should be simple: make using rail as easy as using a truck.A manufacturer does not necessarily need a private siding, a full rake or even the lowest freight rate. It needs dependable delivery at a predictable total logistics cost. In many cases, the winning solution will not be rail versus road, but rail and road working together.India has largely solved the capacity problem in freight rail. The bigger challenge now is commercial. Roads have gained market share because they have aligned themselves more closely with customers' needs and adapted faster to the country's evolving freight geography.The future of freight will not be decided by who can move the most cargo, but who can serve the customer best.Indian Railways has built the infrastructure, now it must build the service model. Only then can it convert freight capacity into freight market share.(The author is Senior Director and Group Head, Consulting, Crisil Intelligence)Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and Egypt will explore the possibility of a trade agreement to boost bilateral trade and investment while safeguarding the interests of farmers, fishermen and small workers in both countries, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday.Speaking in Cairo, Goyal said officials from the two countries would first prepare the terms of reference to define the scope of a possible agreement and identify areas of mutual benefit."Once the terms of reference are set, we'll find out what we can realistically achieve and how much a boost we can get in both investment and trade," Goyal told ANI."We'll also figure out how to do all this without harming each other's farmers or fishermen," he added.He said the discussions would also take into account the impact on small workers and explore areas where the two economies could complement each other.Addressing the India-Egypt Business Forum earlier in the day, Goyal said the two sides would consider whether a preferential trade agreement or a free trade agreement would be more suitable.Goyal expressed confidence that India and Egypt would achieve the bilateral trade target of $12 billion set by the leaders of the two countries. He said both sides were looking to expand trade further."We will definitely meet that bilateral trade target between the two countries. Beyond that, we want to make a bigger leap," he said.Bilateral trade in goods rose 64% year-on-year to $5.04 billion during April-September 2026, according to a commerce ministry release dated November 14.In the 2025-26 financial year, India's goods exports to Egypt stood at $3.87 billion, while imports from the country were valued at $2.60 billion. articles.title: India’s semiconductor industry boom may add over 1 lakh jobs in India in 3 years, with 67,500 openings in 18 months; senior engineers command up to 6 times IT services salaries
articles.summary: India is betting big on the semiconductor industry to drive an important phase of its manufacturing leap and the focus is expected to create over one lakh
articles.body: India is betting big on the semiconductor industry to drive an important phase of its manufacturing leap and the focus is expected to create over one lakh jobs in the coming years.Industry experts estimate over 1 lakh jobs in the next three years through the country’s efforts to build a semiconductor ecosystem of its own.Hiring requirements in the semiconductor industry are also evolving, with recruitment extending beyond conventional chip-design roles.Talent hunt in semiconductor industryAccording to estimates by Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the country’s semiconductor workforce, currently pegged at 25,000, is expected to expand fourfold during this period.Separately, a study by recruitment and staffing firm CIEL HR Services for ET indicates that companies in the sector could add around 67,500 jobs in the next 18 months.Professionals with specialised skills, including process engineering, chip fabrication, chip design, systems engineering and product architecture, can earn four to six times the salaries of IT services professionals with similar experience. The difference is particularly pronounced at the mid-to-senior levels, Ankush Wadhera, partner and managing director at BCG told the financial daily.“The supply of fit-for-role talent is not keeping pace with demand and, as a result, many players are looking outside India for senior talent,” said Wadhera.The US and Southeast Asia have emerged as key destinations for companies seeking experienced professionals, with a significant share of the global talent pool comprising members of the Indian diaspora.“Entry-level and mid-level talent can be easily trained, but it is senior talent that is in acute shortage in the country,” he said.Specialists in focusCompanies are increasingly looking for specialists in process engineering, equipment maintenance, yield management, reliability engineering and advanced packaging, areas that involve high-value technical work.A CIEL HR Services study estimates that India has around 1.5 lakh semiconductor professionals working across chip design, verification, engineering, testing and product development.“About 43% of the workforce has more than 10 years of experience, while nearly three-fourths have over five years of experience,” said Aditya Narayan Mishra, CEO of CIEL HR Services.A study of India’s semiconductor industry, found that Qualcomm has the highest number of current job openings in the sector. AMD ranks second, followed by Nvidia, Synopsys, Applied Materials, Infineon, Cadence and Micron.“For years, India’s semiconductor workforce was almost entirely focused on design,” said Mishra. “Domestic fabrication and packaging units are now creating demand for roles in process engineering, equipment maintenance, yield management, reliability and advanced packaging, which until recently accounted for a negligible share of hiring.”The shortage of skilled professionals remains acute. The study found that for every 100 engineers with expertise in microarchitecture, the semiconductor industry has 135 vacancies to fill.Companies are looking beyond competitors in the semiconductor industry to meet their hiring requirements, increasingly tapping academic institutions and IT services firms for talent. Among the skills in greatest demand are physical design and timing closure, digital design and RTL (register transfer level) coding, and design verification.Employers are also seeking professionals skilled in microarchitecture, emulation, formal verification, embedded systems and silicon bring-up. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++, Verilog and SystemVerilog, which is used for hardware description and verification, is another sought-after skill.For its analysis, CIEL examined semiconductor recruitment trends in India over the 12 months leading up to November 2026. The study covered approximately 45,000 job openings across more than 150 semiconductor companies.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: AT&T's New Settlement Payout Could Net You $5,000 — Here's How
articles.summary: AT&T customers whose personal information was exposed in two data breaches in 2024 are now covered by a $177 million class-action settlement.
articles.body:
Good news for AT&T customers whose personal information was exposed in two data breaches in 2024: you are now covered by a $177 million class-action settlement. Customers who documented eligible financial losses from the breaches could receive as much as $5,000 for the first breach, while a separate class offers up to $2,500 for losses tied to the second incident.

There is, however, a significant catch: the deadline to file a claim has passed. Anyone who didn't submit one by Dec. 18, 2025, can no longer join the settlement. A federal court finally approved the agreement on October 2; meanwhile, AT&T denies any wrongdoing.

The settlement resolves lawsuits pertaining to two separate data incidents. On March 30, 2024, AT&T announced that a data set containing customer information had been released on the dark web. The exposed information included Social Security numbers and other personal details, per the official settlement website .

A second breach was then announced on July 12, 2024. Someone downloaded limited data from an AT&T workspace hosted on a third-party cloud platform, including phone numbers and records regarding calls and texts.

Customers sued, alleging AT&T failed to adequately protect their information. The cases were combined and settled without an admission of liability or wrongdoing.

Who Qualifies? Can You Still Try to File Past the Filing Date?

The first settlement class in the class-action suit covers people in the United States whose information was included in the March incident. The second class covers AT&T account owners, line users or end users whose information was involved in July.

Now, the claim deadline for this settlement was Dec. 18, 2025. Unfortunately, if you didn't submit a claim by that date, you cannot file now or receive a settlement payment in the future. There is no recourse; per Yahoo Finance , the claim period has permanently closed.

If you did file on time, be sure to visit the official AT&T Data Incident Settlement site for updates. The administrator states that valid claimants do not need to take further action while payment processing is pending.

How Much Money Could You Receive, and When?

The $5,000 maximum applies to first-class claimants who can document losses from 2019 or later and show they are traceable to the March breach. The second class allows up to $2,500 for documented losses from April 14, 2024, onward. People in both classes could quality under each, but must use separate documented losses.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid focus on rollout of next generation of reforms for ease of living across sectors (Deregulation 3.0), including in real estate, cabinet
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid focus on rollout of next generation of reforms for ease of living across sectors (Deregulation 3.0), including in real estate, cabinet secretary TV Somanathan has assured a national homebuyers’ body that their suggestions for strengthening legal provisions to protect buyers’ interests would be looked into.The suggestions of the homebuyers’ body include a statutory exit option enabling buyers to secure hassle-free refunds upon cancellation and direct, automatic compensation payouts for project delays to all allottees without requiring individual, time-consuming legal complaints.To protect buyers’ interests, the Forum for People’s Collective Efforts (FPCE) had written to PM Narendra Modi seeking separation of promotion of the real estate sector from regulation in place of a common entity (RERA) carrying out both tasks and had sent a copy to Somanathan. Responding to it, the cabinet secretary replied that the “thoughtful, well-analysed and wide-ranging suggestions” will be taken into consideration.FPCE president Abhay Upadhyay said that following this, they met senior officials in the Cabinet Secretariat and held a detailed discussion, submitting more suggestions. They have suggested provision of a “binding statutory Agreement for Sale” by including it as a schedule to the RERA law. “Builders continue to insert clauses that defeat the Act, and the agreements carrying them are uploaded on the RERA authorities’ websites without scrutiny,” FPCE said.The organisation also suggested setting up of a National Appellate Tribunal for Real Estate, replacing poorly constituted state tribunals, with statutory appeals heard directly by the Supreme Court-based central forum utilising virtual benches to ensure uniform RERA enforcement nationwide and further appeals lying with the Supreme Court. “National tribunal should hear appeals against orders of RERAs and of the adjudicating officers alike; it should sit through virtual benches scaled to caseload so that no homebuyer need travel to Delhi,” it said.Proposing the statutory exit option for buyers, FPCE said that Section 18 of RERA addresses developer’s default and nothing else. A buyer who opts to withdraw for reasons of their own — loss of employment, death of an earning member — has no exit option and forfeits whatever money the builder chooses to withhold. It suggested hassle-free refunds upon cancellation — 100% within one year of booking and a full refund plus SBI savings-rate interest thereafter — preventing builders from withholding up to 75% of buyer payments in such cases.It also suggested periodic audits and independent order scrutiny of RERAs to curb lax, pro-promoter enforcement, alongside placing a non-negotiable Agreement for Sale in a statutory schedule. articles.title: Haven't saved enough for retirement? Wealthy people haven't either.
articles.summary: Wealthy Americans say they will need $2.6 million to feel financially set to retire, according to a new study.
articles.body:
The rich aren't that different from you and me.

They also agonize about having enough money set aside for retirement — even if the amount they need to "retire comfortably" is loftier.

Wealthy Americans say they will need $2.6 million to feel financially set to retire, up 26% from last year, according to a new study from financial services firm HSBC.

That savings target is roughly double the amount that less-wealthy workers aim for.

"For affluent households, it's not simply about accumulating a larger nest egg, but ensuring their wealth can sustain their desired lifestyle over several decades," Jessie Zhu, an HSBC managing director, told Yahoo Finance.

The problem is, wealthy savers are only halfway toward reaching their goal on average. Baby boomers, those nearest to retirement, have hit 74% of their target, while millennials clock in at just 42%.

That trend holds for those lower on the economic ladder, other surveys have found.

About half of workers surveyed by Schroders have less than $500,000 in savings at retirement — including 24% who say it's unlikely they will have $250,000 set aside.

Northwestern Mutual found that nearly half of workers it surveyed don't expect to be financially prepared and believe there's a good chance they'll outlive their savings.

To help fill the coffers, nearly two-thirds of affluent Americans plan to stretch out their earnings years by slowly trimming back their working hours over time, the HSBC data found.

But formal phased retirement programs that offer a reduced or flexible schedule and a lighter workload have been few and far between. Last year, just 7% of firms surveyed by the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM) offered a formal program. A larger share—about 2 in 10— offered an informal arrangement in which workers create their own plan with their manager.

Like wealthier Americans, working longer is the fallback position for most of us. More than 4 in 10 workers expect to work past age 65 or do not plan to retire, according to Transamerica research.

But the harsh reality is that most people retire before they reach 65 due to a health issue, caregiving for an aging relative, or a job loss.

So how much should you be saving? It depends on many variables, including where you live, how expensive your lifestyle is, your health, and your financial obligations.

In general, you should aim to have 10 times your pre-retirement income saved by the time you reach age 67. If you have an annual salary of $100,000, that means $1 million saved by the time you retire.

Kerry Hannon is a Senior Columnist at Yahoo Finance. She is a career and retirement strategist and the author of 14 books, including " Retirement Bites: A Gen X Guide to Securing Your Financial Future, " " In Control at 50+: How to Succeed in the New World of Work ," and "Never Too Old to Get Rich.

articles.body:

Economist Peter Schiff argues that AI investment is the only factor that is keeping U.S. economic growth positive, and removing that spending would result in a recession.

Schiff took to X and argued that "AI CapEx is the only reason GDP is even positive." He linked a recession to easier monetary policy, warning that such measures would be bearish for bonds, but "not bearish for gold, gold miners or silver."

AI CapEx is the only reason GDP is even positive. Take it out and it's a recession. A recession means easy money. Easy money is very bearish for bonds. It's not bearish for gold, gold miners or silver. pic.twitter.com/efRpocqKG9 — Peter Schiff (@PeterSchiff) November 13, 2026

Peter Schiff (@PeterSchiff) November 13, 2026

In another video, he also discussed the "bad" October consumer inflation, arguing that it reflects the Federal Reserve's inability to contain rising prices because the U.S. government cannot afford the high interest rates needed to control inflation. He blamed excessive government spending for the affordability crisis, warning that mounting fiscal pressures could trigger a broader economic collapse, potentially before the next presidential administration. "We're now in the final stages of this collapse," he said, adding, "The whole thing can implode."

Economists Warn of AI-Driven Bubble Risks

Schiff had previously warned that rising borrowing costs could undermine AI investment and expose broader economic weakness. Former Fed adviser Danielle DiMartino Booth has similarly warned that a recession may already be underway, citing falling Treasury yields and mounting credit stress among AI companies. However, a prediction-market analysis showed only a 7% chance of a 2026 recession, although traders assigned greater recession risk to 2027.

Notably, the U.S. economy expanded at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, beating economists' 3.2% forecast and accelerating from 2.2% growth in the second quarter, according to the BEA's advance estimate.

NYU professor Scott Galloway warned that the AI infrastructure boom resembles the 1999 dot-com bubble, arguing that trillions of dollars in data-center and chip investments increasingly depend on demand from just two companies: OpenAI and Anthropic . He cautioned that this concentrated customer base could make the massive AI capital spending vulnerable.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Around 75% of eligible hit-and-run victims and their families miss out on compensation provided in the Motor Vehicles Act, according to a new
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Around 75% of eligible hit-and-run victims and their families miss out on compensation provided in the Motor Vehicles Act, according to a new report based on govt data on hit-and-run cases and compensations disbursed.The report by Primus Partners, a management consultancy firm, revealed that close to 70,000 hit-and-run cases are reported annually on average, claiming over 30,000 lives and leaving another 16,000 people seriously injured. Going by the compensation norm in the MV Act, the total annual compensation, taking into account all cases, should be around Rs 600 crore. However, less than Rs 300 crore has been disbursed in four years, highlighting a stark delivery gap.The updated Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme rolled out in Feb 2022 provides Rs 2 lakh for death and Rs 50,000 for grievous injury.The report said, "As against an annual average 30,000 deaths and 16,000 grievous hurt victims due to hit-and-run accidents, number of claims registered have been less than 10,000 annually. Further, even after registering claims, less than 8,000 claimants have received compensation annually. As a result, less than 25% of Centre's yearly obligation of more than Rs 600 cr was disbursed, even four years after scheme's implementation."The report listed the hurdles, including low awareness and information asymmetry, complex and lengthy process, administrative bottlenecks, redundant disbursal layers and deterrent undertakings. It found that more than 80% of the respondents were completely unaware of the scheme, and 84% of those who knew about it did not know where to find forms or guidelines.It recommended the scheme's implementation through the district police department so that the compensation procedure is initiated suo motu immediately after a road crash is classified as hit and run. To transition to a digital, system-initiated process, it recommended migrating the scheme's implementation to the eDAR platform."Integrating the network of Common Service Centres into the scheme framework could help victims in submitting basic details on eDAR... Apart from transforming the scheme implementation framework, it is also critical to ensure a formula-based annual revision of compensation amount, for which budgetary support or other sources of funds may need to be tapped by the Union govt of India," the report said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Trump, McDonald’s and Burger King among targets of past X posts that contain redirected website links
articles.summary: Some website links included in the X posts of politicians, government agencies and companies were redirected this weekend with unrelated videos, images and websites.
articles.body: Some website links included in the X posts of politicians, government agencies and companies were redirected this weekend to unrelated videos, images and websites. Links dating as far back as 2009 from URL-shortening service Bitly were affected, and only corporate and political X accounts appear to have been targeted, with President Donald Trump’s personal account seemingly hit the hardest. At least a dozen of Trump’s posts on X now direct to various inappropriate and unrelated sites. Public figures — like Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and former Vice President Mike Pence — as well as fast-food chains McDonald’s and Burger King, were also hit to varying degrees. Bitly URLs are shortened while holding the original and longer link. Bitly links do not automatically expire, according to the company’s website, but paid users can redirect links. Bitly said Sunday afternoon in a post on X that it had “identified an issue that allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links to redirect people to content unrelated to the original posts.” The company said it suspended the accounts that altered links and were working to disable the affected URLs. “Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the issue and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote. Both Bitly and X have not yet responded to CNN’s request for comment. It’s unclear whether hackers made custom Bitly links, which effectively allow them to copy the original URL and redirect to any website. That may have been possible if the original Bitly link to the website no longer exists or has expired. Bitly links may be susceptible to artificial intelligence scans and exploiting mechanisms to redirect links, noted Ari Lightman, a digital media professor at Carnegie Mellon University’s Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy. The redirected links seem confined to posts made between 2009 and 2014. Lightman said that some social media accounts are not monitored, “and that’s problematic.” Changing unmonitored links could expose user information when clicking those links, he warned, highlighting the importance of internet safety. “You have a variety of vulnerabilities that people can utilize for exploitation,” said Lightman. “It’s just finding these old messages out there and sort of repopulating them,” often for malicious purposes. A 2013 post from Trump criticizing wind turbines that used a Bitly link now redirects to a Google site titled “fortnite baby” and includes a photo of a baby. Another 2013 post from Trump tagged former Republican nominee for president Mitt Romney, and links to the popular game “Geometry Dash.” One of Trump’s posts about his golf course in Scotland includes a link to an Epstein files Wikipedia page. “It sounds like they’re trying to make some sort of a message tying these sites into Donald Trump’s policies, and sometimes it’s just vulgar mechanisms,” said Lightman. Public officials and company heads who often circulated Bitly links were also targeted. A post in 2010 from Microsoft founder Bill Gates contains the text, “Notes from D.C. trip. Spoke w/former President Clinton at the Foreign Relations committee aid programs are working,” and includes a Bitly link of a Reddit page that has an animated image from a fabricated posting by former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg. A post in 2011 by Trudeau contains a Bitly link that redirects to a vulgar YouTube audio clip. A 2011 post from Burger King intended to provide restaurant locations was redirected to a Wikipedia page on a list of Nazi concentration camps, while another post linked to a Wikipedia page on Adolf Hitler. McDonald’s account has a post from 2011 that redirected to a page about the September 11 attacks, while its Indonesia account made a 2013 post about a jingle that now links to an unrelated “Would you rather?” YouTube video. A spokesperson for Burger King told CNN the company has “no part in the links being redirected” and that it was “working quickly to correct and delete posts that have been altered.” McDonald’s did not immediately respond to CNN’s request for comment. Government accounts have also been ironically affected. A 2012 post from the FBI about computers infected by “Ghost Clicks” now directs to a page with a photo of a seal, while the Department of Defense account had a separately redirected post. A post by Pence seemingly directed to the same website as the FBI, despite being about an unrelated topic. Hijacking these links is especially concerning in the age of AI, says Lightman, because it allows manipulations to be made “en masse.”

articles.title: Futuristic Shenzhen Shows Trump the Difficulty of Stopping China
articles.summary: The city hosting APEC this week embodies Xi Jinping’s tech ambitions — and the economic woes lurking beneath.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Under the towering skyscrapers home to some of China's biggest tech giants, a small group of foreigners tilt up their smartphones to capture a drone descending from the Shenzhen sky with a fresh serving of bubble tea.

They've paid around $90 a head to be dazzled by the southern Chinese city's tech wonders on a tour led by Sean Zhang, who returned home in 2023 after studying in California. He's now cashing in as tourists flock to Shenzhen to experience frontier technologies like flying robotaxis, wearable exoskeletons and buildings shaped like giant AirPods. Influencers on Western social media platforms regularly post videos with titles like "China built a city that feels like 2050!"

"Shenzhen usually leaves a very good impression," says Zhang, 27, who has more than doubled the number of tours offered over the past year. "Many walk away saying: 'This isn't what I expected of China.'"

It's that innovation President Xi Jinping wants to show the world — and Donald Trump — when he hosts the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit this week in this city of some 18 million people. At the turn of the century, Shenzhen was best known for its cheap knock-offs of Western goods. Today, the city's progress serves as a powerful symbol of China's technological rise — and the limits of Washington's efforts to hold it back.

Dozens of companies in Shenzhen, including national tech champion Huawei Technologies Co. and Tencent Holdings Ltd., are on US blacklists designed to restrict their access to American exports and markets. But that hasn't stopped them going from strength to strength. BYD Co. last year dethroned US giant Tesla Inc. as the world's top supplier of electric vehicles, while SZ DJI Technology Co. now controls about 70% of the global consumer drone market.

That boom has made Shenzhen a bright spot even as it epitomizes the broader paradox in China's economy: While exports are surging and its tech companies are becoming global leaders, many locals aren't feeling any richer as wage growth slows and many firms struggle to eke out profits.

Shenzhen saw the highest population growth rate of any major Chinese city last year, and has one of the country's youngest average urban populations at 32.5 years old. Airport signs declare: "Once Here Shenzhener Forever." While China has a glut of unsold real estate — Goldman Sachs Group Inc. estimated in 2024 it would be worth $13 trillion if fully built — the city is actually seeing a supply squeeze, making it potentially the first place to climb out of the nation's five-year property slump.

articles.title: Oil Steadies With Iranian Attack on Base in Bahrain in Focus
articles.summary: Oil steadied after a two-week slump, as fresh attacks in the Middle East countered signs of a well-supplied physical market.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Oil steadied after a two-week slump, as fresh attacks in the Middle East countered signs of a well-supplied physical market.

Brent held below $96 a barrel after falling more than 2% last week, while West Texas Intermediate was near $89. Iran targeted a US helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday in its first strike on a Persian Gulf state in weeks, with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps saying it launched drones at the facility.

Iranian state TV, meanwhile, said five vessels struck mines and caught fire in the past 48 hours, without identifying them. UK Maritime Trade Operations said Indian shipping authorities reported an attack on a tanker in the gulf and the crew were safe, although the extent of the damage was unknown.

Oil has tumbled this month, with the Trump administration yet to restart airstrikes against Iran following the Democratic sweep at the US midterm elections. The International Energy Agency said last week that global oil supply exceeded demand for the first time since the war began, with an expected overhang of roughly 2 million barrels a day this quarter. That shift reflects a revival of energy flows through the still-contested Strait of Hormuz.

Despite the attack on the base in Bahrain, Iran reiterated that a path to ending the conflict remained open, with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf saying the war could end if Washington accepted Tehran's "logical conditions". President Donald Trump has said further attacks against the Islamic Republic wouldn't be necessary, though the US remained "locked and loaded".

The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier arrived in the Central Command area of responsibility on Sunday, an Axios reporter said in a post on X, citing a US official. Washington now has three aircraft carrier strike groups in the Centcom area, he said. The war began in February, when the US and Israel launched a joint attack against Iran to combat its nuclear program.

articles.title: Domestic demand, industry, earnings power growth in Q2
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: On the back of resilient domestic demand, steady industrial activity and strong corporate earnings, the economy is projected to have sustained
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On the back of resilient domestic demand, steady industrial activity and strong corporate earnings, the economy is projected to have sustained its growth momentum in the Sept quarter of the current financial year, with a TOI poll of 10 economists projecting real GDP expansion of 7.5% or more, following the 7.8% print recorded during April-June.In its latest monetary policy review last month, RBI projected Sept quarter growth at 7.2%, with the finance ministry's monthly economic review pegging it at 7.35%. The National Statistical Office (NSO) is scheduled to release the official GDP data for the second quarter on Nov 30.Based on its 54 high-frequency indicators across agriculture, industry and services, SBI expects Q2 growth to have been 7.8%, with nominal GDP expected to grow 11-11.5%, up from 10.3% in the June quarter.DK Joshi of Crisil, too, estimated GDP to have grown at a similar pace during the quarter. "All the underlying data across sectors point to this, along with robust tax collection numbers."Both IDFC First Bank chief economist Gaura Sengupta and Emkay Global economist Madhavi Arora expect Q2 growth to track around 8%, slightly higher than the June quarter. Sengupta noted that the momentum is led by manufacturing, with factory output growing 8.1% in Q2, alongside rising listed company profits due to strong sales outpacing input cost pressures. "Robust corporate tax and GST collections further corroborate the trend," she said.DBS Bank senior economist Radhika Rao and HDFC Bank chief economist Sakshi Gupta projected Q2 growth at 7.7%, while CareEdge Ratings chief economist Rajani Sinha estimated it at 7.6%. Sinha pointed out that manufacturing drew strength from auto sales and core (non-oil, non-gold) exports, while front-loaded public capex, particularly steady state capex supported construction, despite a moderation in the centre's capex due to an adverse base."Services, however, presented a mixed bag as bank credit and services exports held firm, whereas air passenger traffic contracted deeper due to higher fares triggered by the West Asia conflict, alongside moderation in aviation turbine fuel (ATF) consumption and e-way bills," said Sinha.ICRA chief economist Aditi Nayar and Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis project growth at 7.5% and 7.4%, respectively. "If Q2 growth exceeds our target, a larger repo rate hike of 50bps may be on the cards," said Nayar, amid inflation rising to 6.1%.India Ratings chief economist DK Pant is the most conservative in his estimation, suggesting of at least 7% in Q2, with expectations of a softening urban consumption in coming months.Economists pointed to the gaps in rural consumption, as evident in the surge in employment demand under the VB-G RAM G scheme alongside softer tractor and two-wheeler sales, with the brunt of a weak monsoon expected during the second half of financial year.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Loan repayment cap for MFIs to stay: RBI
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI has made it clear that microfinance institutions cannot allow borrowers' total monthly loan repayments to exceed 50% of their household
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI has made it clear that microfinance institutions cannot allow borrowers' total monthly loan repayments to exceed 50% of their household income, rejecting an industry proposal to relax the cap by excluding principal repayments from the calculation.The regulator, however, is open to reviewing the Rs 3 lakh annual household income ceiling for microfinance eligibility, depending on industry developments and its assessment of the need for a revision. "Excluding some loans from the calculation would defeat this purpose, tinker with the sanctity of the limit and understate household leverage," RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu said.Under RBI's 2022 regulatory framework, households with an annual income of up to Rs 3 lakh are eligible for microfinance loans from regulated lenders. Their total monthly loan repayments across lenders cannot exceed 50% of household income.Known as the Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR), the measure captures the proportion of a household's monthly income committed to servicing loans. For instance, if a household earns Rs 20,000 a month, its combined monthly repayments across loans cannot exceed Rs 10,000. Both principal and interest payments are included.Microfinance lenders had sought a more accommodative interpretation that would exclude the principal component of certain loans and count only interest payments. This would have reduced the repayment burden recorded under FOIR and created room for lenders to extend additional credit without breaching the 50% ceiling.Murmu said the objective of the cap was to prevent over-indebtedness, while ensuring that a reasonable share of household income remained available for essential consumption and other living expenses. He said 50% was already a liberal threshold given the limited financial cushion of low-income households and their vulnerability to economic shocks.Citing a recent study, he said the average microfinance borrower spends 18.7% of monthly household income on loan repayments, while close to two-thirds goes towards consumption. NABARD's rural economic conditions and sentiments surveys showed a similar pattern, with consumption and other expenses accounting for roughly three-fourths of monthly household income."In such a scenario, an accommodative view on FOIR may be uncalled for," Murmu said, adding that the regulatory FOIR should be treated as a prudential maximum and not a target that every household has to meet.On Rs 3 lakh annual household income threshold, Murmu said a review would be undertaken depending on RBI's assessment of the need for a revision and developments in the industry.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Food items see price escalation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Resurgence in the price of food items like rice, pulses, vegetables, sugar, fruits, coarse grains and protein rich items like meat and fish is
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Resurgence in the price of food items like rice, pulses, vegetables, sugar, fruits, coarse grains and protein rich items like meat and fish is bound to impact the living costs for households. Far from a localised blip in inflation, a TOI analysis of NSO data reveals a sweeping price escalation across the nearly 200-odd food items ledger.DHouseholds which saw price relief earlier this year are now essentially facing a U-turn as prices for both the staples and other daily use items continue to rise, as headline retail inflation touched 6.09% in Oct, crossing RBI's 6% red line for the first time under the new base series, driven by a widespread firestorm in the food basket which had pushed food inflation to 8.9% in the month.Data shows prices of staple rice (12.5%), millets (38%), jowar (18.7%) and vegetables such as onions (116%), garlic (60%) and ginger (48%) have swung vigorously by Oct from a contraction zone recorded earlier this year. Pulses like arhar (15%), urad (11.6%), gram (7.4%) and fruits such as banana (11%), papaya (15%), lemon (48%), apple (18%) and litchi (17%) also mirror this swing.Protein-rich food items such as chicken (11.3%) and egg (8.3%) saw slight price deceleration in Oct, yet remained high. Buffalo meat (15.3%) and fish (8.5%) prices accelerated further during the month. Cooking mediums which include edible oils such as refined oil (16%), groundnut oil (16.5%), and mustard oil (9.8%), along with spices - dry chillies (23%), coriander (22%) and turmeric (8%) also felt the price pinch.Domestic cost-of-living squeeze is bleeding into the broader macro economy, with dining out becoming significantly more expensive as restaurants and accommodation services inflation jumped to 10% in Oct, driven by a price rise in cooked snacks and limited-service cafes. Transport costs ticked further during the month, on the back of surging domestic airfares (43.2%) and steady inflation in petrol (7.5%) and diesel (8.4%) prices.Money habits form by age 7.
