articles.title: Anac registra 211 casos de indisciplina após regra que pune má conduta de passageiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Regra para punir má conduta de passageiros entrou em vigor em setembro. Do total, 179 casos foram classificados como atos de indisciplina, 31 como graves e um como gravíssimo.
articles.summary: Regra para punir má conduta de passageiros entrou em vigor em setembro. Do total, 179 casos foram classificados como atos de indisciplina, 31 como graves e um como gravíssimo.
articles.body:
A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) registrou 211 ocorrências envolvendo passageiros indisciplinados desde setembro , quando entraram em vigor as novas regras para punir esse tipo de comportamento no transporte aéreo.

Desse total, 179 foram classificados como atos de indisciplina, 31 como graves e um como gravíssimo. A regulamentação prevê multa de até R$ 17,5 mil e, nos casos mais extremos, suspensão do direito de embarcar em voos domésticos por até um ano.

Entre os casos enquadrados como atos de indisciplina, 74 ocorreram com a aeronave em solo e 66 em áreas de embarque ou desembarque. Houve ainda 18 registros durante o check-in, 11 com a aeronave em voo e oito em canais de inspeção. Outros dois episódios ocorreram em locais não especificados.

A Anac informou que não possui informações detalhadas sobre os aeroportos ou localidades onde as ocorrências foram registradas.

As normas criaram uma escala de punições que vai desde advertências e orientações ao passageiro até a proibição temporária de utilizar voos comerciais domésticos.

Nos casos mais graves, o infrator poderá ser incluído em uma lista nacional de passageiros impedidos de embarcar, conhecida como " no-fly list". O cadastro será compartilhado entre todas as companhias que operam voos domésticos regulares no país.

✈️ O termo em inglês "no-fly list" designa uma relação oficial de pessoas proibidas de embarcar em aeronaves comerciais.

🛫 Nos casos mais leves, o passageiro receberá orientação. Nessa categoria estão situações como descumprir instruções da tripulação, ignorar orientações em solo, utilizar aparelhos eletrônicos quando proibido, provocar tumulto ou ofender outras pessoas durante a viagem.

Condutas que representem maior risco à ordem das operações ou à segurança do voo poderão ser enquadradas como atos graves.

Nesses casos, a Anac prevê multa de até R$ 17,5 mil, além do encerramento do contrato de transporte firmado com a companhia aérea . Entre as infrações consideradas graves estão agressões verbais a funcionários ou passageiros, fumar a bordo, danificar equipamentos da aeronave e ameaçar membros da tripulação.

Já os atos gravíssimos podem resultar, além da multa e do cancelamento da viagem, na suspensão do direito de voar por seis meses ou um ano.

Entram nessa categoria agressões físicas à tripulação, adulteração de equipamentos de segurança, atentado contra a dignidade sexual, transporte irregular de armas ou explosivos, tentativa de invasão da cabine de comando e ações destinadas a assumir o controle da aeronave.

Durante o período de suspensão, o passageiro ficará impedido de embarcar em voos domésticos regulares . As companhias aéreas terão de bloquear a emissão de passagens, impedir o check-in e negar o embarque.

Para garantir o cumprimento da medida, a resolução determina a criação de um sistema de compartilhamento de informações entre as empresas aéreas , permitindo que a restrição seja aplicada em toda a malha aérea doméstica.

A norma também prevê multa de R$ 70 mil para companhias que deixarem de aplicar a suspensão quando a medida for obrigatória.

Movimento de passageiros no Aeroporto Internacional de Guarulhos, o maior do País, localizado em Guarulhos, na Região Metropolitana de São Paulo, nesta terça-feira, 14. — Foto: FELIPE RAU/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

As regras também definem que as companhias aéreas e operadores aeroportuários devem informar à Anac todos os casos de indisciplina registrados em suas áreas de atuação.

Nos episódios classificados como gravíssimos, a comunicação deverá ser imediata . Para infrações graves, o prazo será de até cinco dias após a ocorrência. Nos demais casos, a notificação pode ser feita em até 30 dias.

Segundo a agência, a fiscalização será realizada por meio de um sistema administrado pelo Serpro, que permitirá monitorar tanto a aplicação das sanções aos passageiros quanto o cumprimento das obrigações impostas a companhias aéreas e operadores aeroportuários.

As regras valem para todo o transporte aéreo regular doméstico, incluindo trechos nacionais conectados a voos internacionais, observadas as exceções previstas em lei e as normas específicas aplicáveis às operações internacionais.

articles.title: Bolsa Família 2026: pagamentos de novembro começam nesta segunda; veja calendário | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiros a receber serão os beneficiários com Número de Identificação Social (NIS) com final 1. Pagamento mínimo previsto é de R$ 691 por família, com possíveis adicionais.
articles.summary: Primeiros a receber serão os beneficiários com Número de Identificação Social (NIS) com final 1.  Pagamento mínimo previsto é de R$ 691 por família, com possíveis adicionais.
articles.body:
A Caixa Econômica Federal inicia os pagamentos de novembro do Bolsa Família 2026 nesta segunda-feira (16). Os primeiros a receber serão os beneficiários com Número de Identificação Social (NIS) com final 1.

Este é o segundo mês de pagamentos com os valores reajustados pelo governo. Anunciado em 17 de setembro , o aumento elevou o piso do Bolsa Família de R$ 600 para R$ 691 e também ampliou os benefícios complementares. (leia mais abaixo)

🤔 Para saber a data correta de recebimento, a família deve verificar o último dígito do NIS , impresso no cartão do programa. Assim, é possível consultar o dia correspondente no calendário oficial de pagamentos.

Em outubro, o governo federal anunciou a antecipação dos pagamentos do Bolsa Família para os últimos meses do ano, sob a justificativa de reduzir os impactos do super El Niño sobre as famílias mais vulneráveis. (entenda abaixo)

O dinheiro costuma ser disponibilizado nos últimos 10 dias úteis de cada mês, de forma escalonada. A exceção é o mês de dezembro, quando os pagamentos são antecipados. Com a mudança, porém, ficaram concentrados em apenas três dias.

Veja como ficou o calendário do Bolsa Família para novembro de 2026:

16/11: pagamentos para NIS com final 1 ;

17/11: pagamentos para NIS com final 2 ;

18/11: pagamentos para NIS com finais 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 e 0 .

O governo federal explicou que a unificação foi adotada para outubro, novembro e dezembro , meses em que o Super El Niño pode intensificar seus efeitos no país.

Veja abaixo perguntas e respostas sobre o Bolsa Família.

Bolsa Família — Foto: Luis Lima Jr/FotoArena/Estadão Conteúdo

A principal regra para receber o benefício é ter renda mensal familiar de até R$ 218 por pessoa.

Para se enquadrar do programa, é preciso somar a renda total e dividir pelo número de pessoas. Caso o valor fique abaixo dos R$ 218 , a família está elegível ao Bolsa Família.

Os beneficiários também precisam arcar com contrapartidas, como:

manter crianças e adolescentes na escola;

fazer o acompanhamento pré-natal (no caso de gestantes);

manter as carteiras de vacinação atualizadas.

Com a mudança anunciada pelo governo , o Bolsa Família passou a prever o pagamento mínimo de R$ 691 por família.

A medida também elevou de R$ 142 para R$ 164 o chamado Benefício de Renda de Cidadania . Esse é o valor pago por integrante da família pelo programa.

🔎 Se uma família elegível tiver três pessoas , por exemplo, a soma será de R$ 492 (3 × R$ 164). Como o valor fica abaixo do piso, a família receberá o complemento necessário para chegar a R$ 691.

🔎 Já uma família de cinco pessoas terá como base R$ 820 (5 × R$ 164).

Além do piso, há benefícios complementares, que também foram reajustados:

R$ 173 por criança de até 6 anos (eram R$ 150);

R$ 58 por criança ou adolescente de 7 a 17 anos (eram R$ 50);

R$ 58 por bebê de até 6 meses (eram R$ 50).

Na prática, portanto, o valor recebido por cada família varia conforme sua composição e pode aumentar com os benefícios adicionais para crianças, adolescentes e gestantes.

Os beneficiários precisam se inscrever no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico) — principal instrumento do governo federal para a inclusão de famílias de baixa renda em programas sociais — e aguardar uma análise de enquadramento.

Estar no Cadastro Único não significa a entrada automática nos programas sociais do governo, uma vez que cada um deles tem regras específicas. Mas o cadastro é pré-requisito para que a inscrição seja avaliada.

Os beneficiários recebem e podem movimentar os valores pelo aplicativo Caixa TEM e internet banking . Assim, não é necessário ir até uma agência da Caixa Econômica Federal — que é responsável pelo pagamento do Bolsa Família — para realizar o saque.

Segundo a Caixa, os beneficiários também podem utilizar o cartão do programa para realizar compras nos estabelecimentos comerciais, por meio da função de débito.

Além disso, há a opção de realizar saques nos terminais de autoatendimento, casas lotéricas e correspondentes Caixa Aqui, além das agências da Caixa.

articles.title: Prejuízo dos Correios chega a R$ 7,5 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Prejuízo até setembro de 2026 somou R$ 7,5 bilhões, segundo balanço da empresa; estatal está em reestruturação de seu modelo de negócios
articles.summary: O prejuízo dos Correios atingiu R$ 7,5 bilhões até setembro de 2026, impulsionado pela concorrência e custos, exigindo um plano de reestruturação da estatal.
articles.body:
Correios acumula trimestres de prejuízo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Com o prejuízo de R$ 7,5 bilhões registrado até o terceiro trimestre de 2026 , os Correios chegaram a seu 16º trimestre seguido de contas no vermelho.

O valor registrado até setembro de 2026 representa um aumento no prejuízo registrado no mesmo período de 2025. No ano passado, até o fim do terceiro trimestre, os Correios fecharam as contas R$ 5,9 bilhões no negativo.

Os resultados atuais também representam um aumento no rombo já registrado no primeiro semestre. Na época, o prejuízo era de R$ 5,6 bilhões.

Segundo a estatal, há "pressões relevantes" para seus resultados nos últimos meses. Entre elas:

aumento da concorrência no setor de logística;

queda nas receitas de serviços postais tradicionais;

manutenção da estrutura dos Correios em todo o país ; e

Apesar desse cenário, os Correios afirmam que o resultado até setembro de 2026 veio R$ 272 milhões melhor do que o esperado — ou seja, o rombo previsto era maior.

O demonstrativo financeiro mostra que a receita total da empresa no terceiro trimestre chegou a R$ 13,2 bilhões. Já as despesas somaram R$ 20,7 bilhões, cerca de 1,2% abaixo do planejado.

A maior parte da receita dos Correios teve como origem serviços e vendas oferecidos pela empresa. Foram R$ 11,7 bilhões recebidos dessa forma. Ainda assim, houve queda de 5,33% na comparação com os resultados do mesmo período de 2025.

"Os indicadores de receitas e despesas mostram que os resultados seguem em linha com o planejamento para 2026", diz a estatal em nota. Os Correios atualmente têm um plano de reestruturação para tentar recuperar suas contas.

A estatal reconhece a necessidade de um "acompanhamento" de suas contas, em especial pela quantidade de resultados negativos acumulados nos últimos meses. A administração dos Correios fala ainda na "necessidade de recuperação sustentável" de seu caixa.

Para tentar lidar com essas pressões, os Correios aprovaram no fim de 2025 um plano de reestruturação. O plano reúne três eixos principais:

Com ações até 2027, a estratégia é reorganizar a empresa para diminuir custos e modernizar seu modelo de negócios. Segundo a estatal, os resultados dessas ações têm "diferentes prazos" e devem ser observados somente no futuro.

"O monitoramento do Plano de Reestruturação evidencia a evolução da implementação das iniciativas destinadas ao aumento da eficiência operacional, à recuperação da competitividade e ao fortalecimento da capacidade de geração de receitas", diz o relatório contábil.

Ainda segundo o documento, uma das prioridades dos Correios no momento é manter a liquidez da empresa enquanto o plano é colocado em prática. Para isso, em outubro deste ano — depois dos resultados do terceiro trimestre —, a estatal conseguiu a autorização formal para o empréstimo de R$ 7 bilhões, anunciado ainda nos resultados do segundo semestre .

O empréstimo conta com garantia do governo federal. Com sua concretização, os Correios chegaram a R$ 19 bilhões em empréstimos desde o fim de 2025.

A nova quantia bilionária tinha previsão de entrar no caixa da estatal somente no início de novembro, segundo o relatório contábil.

"A contratação representa avanço relevante na execução da estratégia de financiamento da Empresa, contribuindo para o fortalecimento das perspectivas de liquidez e para a sustentação financeira das operações durante o período de implementação das medidas de reestruturação", diz o documento.

articles.title: After MNCs, domestic companies embrace GCC model
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Global capability centres (GCCs), initially set up by MNCs in India to tap skilled talent, lower operating costs and manage global operations
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Global capability centres (GCCs), initially set up by MNCs in India to tap skilled talent, lower operating costs and manage global operations more efficiently, are finding growing acceptance among Indian businesses too. From conglomerates to companies with overseas operations, domestic firms are creating dedicated centres to bring technology, finance and human resources under one roof, reflecting a shift towards centralised operations.Top conglomerates including Adani, Tata and Mahindra, have adopted the model to integrate operations, standardise processes and drive digitisation across their businesses.While no specific number capturing the rising trend is available yet, multiple companies and industry experts confirmed to TOI that adoption is gathering pace across sectors.India has 2,117 GCCs employing around 2.36 million professionals, according to the Nasscom-Zinnov FY26 report. Most are MNC-led, with mandates extending beyond cost arbitrage to technology, AI, engineering and product development.Says Bhanu Prakash Kalmath SJ, healthcare industry leader, Grant Thornton Bharat: As businesses become more global, digitally intensive and organisationally complex, dedicated capability centres can give strategic leverage and consolidate functions otherwise dispersed across business units or external providers, while building common technology platforms, retaining institutional knowledge, strengthening innovation and creating deeper pools of specialist talent, while delivering efficiency''.Indian conglomerates, which have global operations have also been adopting the model to drive up efficiency and competitive advantage, adds Shalini Pillay, India leader - GCC, KPMG India. The trend is also spread to mid-sized companies with service providers helping them to establish and scale such centres.Some groups are taking this a step further by commercialising capabilities developed for captive internal use. For instance, Strides Pharma's Arcolab, which began as a captive shared-services organisation, evolved into Pivot Path recently.Companies such as ITC, Tata Steel and the JSW Group have captive shared-services centres supporting their wider businesses. Separately, ITC Infotech has set up a Future Capability Centre for a UK-based client, and is helping other companies establish GCCs.Further, the pharmaceutical sector has adopted the trend, particularly among domestic companies with sizeable international operations. Domestic companies are increasingly exploring the GCC model to achieve scale and tap into innovation, taking a cue from MNCs that have expanded their GCC operations, said Sujay Shetty, global health industries advisory leader, PwC India.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites
articles.summary: By Joey Roulette Nov 15 (Reuters) - A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed on Sunday shortl...
articles.body:
Nov 15 (Reuters) - A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed on Sunday shortly after liftoff from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites from Amazon's Leo internet network in the launch company's first mission failure.

The rocket failed ‌roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, and the cause was not immediately clear. It represented a major ‌setback for the two-decade-old company's new flagship rocket as ULA sought to begin a regular cadence of launches for Amazon's burgeoning satellite internet constellation.

"Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan ​vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a statement.

"Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something. Since the anomaly just occurred, we don't have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today," ULA said.

The failure is expected to lead to a lengthy technical investigation that would keep the rocket off the market for months. This could deepen a US launch bottleneck brought on by other rocket mishaps and challenges across ‌the industry as well as the looming retirement of SpaceX's ⁠Falcon 9, the world's most active rocket. SpaceX is no longer accepting bookings for the Falcon 9.

"There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01," Amazon said in a statement, referring to the name of Sunday's mission. "ULA has been ⁠a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they'll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan."

The Sunday flight was Vulcan's fifth since its 2024 debut and first in nine months, following a launch hiatus drawn out by separate technical investigations into its solid rocket side boosters and its core BE-4 engines, which are supplied by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue ​Origin ​space company.

Blue Origin is working with ULA in the investigation into Sunday's failure, according to a ​person familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The ‌boosters were being scrutinized for issues encountered on Vulcan's last two flights, including a mission in February for the US Space Force. Both missions successfully delivered their payloads to orbit, but the Pentagon had not yet approved the rocket to resume flying national security payloads, pending its performance with the Amazon mission on Sunday.

articles.title: Indian liqueur cos carve out space with new flavours
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Indian liqueur makers are looking beyond conventional flavours and imported labels to carve out a space alongside global names such as Kahlua,
articles.body: BENGALURU: Indian liqueur makers are looking beyond conventional flavours and imported labels to carve out a space alongside global names such as Kahlua, Baileys and Tia Maria. From spice-led liqueurs and traditional herbal infusions to coffee blends, they are turning local flavours into contemporary drinks, hoping to build curiosity and repeat purchases.Rajasthan's heritage liqueur maker Maharani Mahansar draws on recipes from Mahansar's erstwhile royal family. MD Surendra Pratap Singh traces his family's tradition to 1768. The family resumed commercial production in 2005. Ingredients include Pushkar roses, Kerala cardamom and oranges from Nagpur.He says the country liquor tag makes Indians associate traditional drinks with cheap alcohol. "We have always felt our own things were inferior," he said. Younger buyers and women are changing his business. Rose has overtaken fennel, accounting for 50-60% of sales. He put FY26 turnover at Rs 80 crore.Palasa, a cream liqueur, launched in Delhi late October. Former market researcher Lekshmi Krishnan developed its Indian blend of saffron, rose, cardamom, nuts and fruit. It is mixed with Dutch cream and bottled in the Netherlands.She says "these are all ingredients that, you know, we all know and love."Goa-based Quaffine began commercial operations in September 2022. Co-founder Olson Pereira, a former bartender, drew on Chennai's filter coffee for the cold-brew liqueur. The recipe took about 11 months to develop during the pandemic. He sees specialty coffee culture and espresso martinis helping create demand. "Our tutor is Instagram today," he said, describing how consumers discover cocktails.Bandarful, a cold-brew coffee liqueur launched in 2024 by Uttarakhand's Himmaleh Spirits, uses Chikmagalur beans and Himalayan spring water. It sells in Delhi, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Goa. "We believe the origin adds to the appeal, but ultimately, the taste has to deliver," the company said.Familiar ingredients can resonate at home while offering "a touch of the exotic for international audience," said Vikram Achanta, co-founder of beverage consultancy Tulleeho. There is a practical opening, too. Pereira recalls switching between imported coffee liqueurs because "the supply was inconsistent." Achanta says that dependable availability lets bars commit to cocktails using a particular brand.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: What a Tiny Chorus of the ‘Bring Back Jensen’ Tech Bros Gets Wrong
articles.summary: Nvidia's board did not fold to a woke mob. It woke up to a national security problem it had been negligent on – with devastating consequences.
articles.body:
A small band of rogue tech bros has ridden to Jensen Huang's defense amidst a report from the Financial Times that Huang is huddling with allies, plotting a comeback as Nvidia CEO days after resigning, with a petition demanding "due process, not mob justice," signed by a minority of tech voices who have gotten outsized attention, such as Elon Musk and Atreides Management managing partner Gavin Baker. One tech bro even said , "Nvidia would be wrong to fire Jensen. His marital indiscretions are between him, his wife, and a reprimand from the board," as if that was all there is to the story.

But this small circle of rogue tech bros is wrong. This is not a story about a woke inquisition or prudes regulating marital indiscretions and sex – and a Sam Altman-style comeback does not make sense. We were supportive of Altman's comeback and knew Steve Jobs personally – and supported his firing and subsequent comeback . But these circumstances are materially different. There is no comeback here.

Start with the conduct the defenders wave away, of Huang's workplace affairs with direct subordinates. Huang admitted infidelity on Nov. 8. Days later, the New York Times reported a relationship with one of his direct reports. Nvidia's code of conduct , which opens with a letter from Huang himself, names "personal relationships" as a conflict of interest. We had firsthand knowledge of Mark Hurd's removal at HP over expense reports that concealed a personal relationship with a contractor, which was the right removal. Boards at McDonald's, Intel and Nestlé similarly removed CEOs over relationships with employees. Workplace romances with bosses having affairs with married direct reports put those subordinates in an inherently compromised position; they are deleterious to the morale of those around them, raising questions of merit and favoritism.

But when it comes to Huang and Nvidia's woes, workplace romance is the least of it. The relationship that should alarm Americans the most was Nvidia's "culture of noncompliance" on chip export restrictions to China, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put it on Sunday with Larry Kudlow, irrespective of whether or not Alice Huang, who helped set up Megaspeed, was an actual Chinese spy. As Bessent said, was Nvidia "pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?"

Evidence points to a fifth or more of Nvidia 's compute revenue being tied to China

The paper trail when it comes to banned Nvidia chips illegally making their way into China at scale, evading U.S. restrictions, is particularly damning for the company.

articles.title: Sebi to issue guidelines for usage of AI in markets: Pandey

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sebi will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the capital markets, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said, emphasising the need to balance technological innovation with investor protection.The Sebi chief said the proposed guidelines would focus on establishing appropriate guardrails for AI use, including disclosures, accountability of regulated entities and a 'human-in-the-loop' approach to ensure that critical decisions are subject to human oversight.In June 2025, Sebi floated a consultation paper proposing guiding principles for responsible usage of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) applications/models in securities markets.These guiding principles are intended to optimise benefits and minimise potential risks associated with the integration of AI/ML based applications in securities markets to safeguard investor protection, market integrity, and financial stability.Speaking at the inauguration of Sebi's pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, Pandey said the regulator has been continuously strengthening its cybersecurity framework to address rising cyber threats.He highlighted growing concerns over cyberattacks targeting financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, as well as digital frauds involving social media influencers. articles.title: Nvidia stock steady as Jensen Huang reportedly weighs CEO comeback, Musk backs return
articles.summary: Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing a comeback as supporters in Silicon Valley lobby for his return.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock futures were little changed on Sunday evening as investors digested a report that supporters of Jensen Huang are lobbying for his return to the AI chip giant following his abrupt resignation last week.

Huang has discussed returning as CEO with confidants, the Financial Times reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang resigned last week following reports of affairs, including one with a woman who was reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy.

According to the report, a Huang supporter said that a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives was being assembled to lobby Nvidia's board to reinstate him, including by seeking support from the White House.

"Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that Huang supported the effort.

Meanwhile, SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk has come out in support of Huang, writing on X last Friday , "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen, and I'm signing it too."

On Saturday, Musk said , "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract. Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

The push to bring Huang back comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached Arm Holdings ( ARM ) CEO Rene Haas as it searches for a successor. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO during the search.

Yorkville's Dan Ives said that while "no one individual can replace Jensen as CEO," any talk of "Jensen coming back to Nvidia is ridiculous in our view given the legal/Board/DC scrutiny/moral compass/China tentacles."

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Huang abruptly stepped down Thursday following reports of alleged affairs with a former executive from Singapore-based Megaspeed, and also an Nvidia employee who reported directly to him.

Exactly one week earlier, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose how many affairs he had or identify those involved.

Recent reports have raised concerns about whether restricted semiconductors were being diverted to China and if sensitive US information had been sent to Beijing.

The developments have also sent shockwaves through the AI industry, where Nvidia has played a central role in building the ecosystem. The company has become a bellwether for the AI trade and has invested in key parts of the industry, including large language model development, energy, optics, and cloud providers.

Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results Tuesday after the bell, in what will be the company's first earnings call without Huang.

The stock declined more than 12% last week, closing below a $4 trillion market cap. At least 10 Wall Street analysts have downgraded the stock from Buy to Hold, with many citing, in part, increased scrutiny in Washington and succession uncertainty.

articles.title: US flight chaos continues: 2,400 flights cancelled, 8,800 delayed as recovery drags on
articles.summary: US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third
articles.body: US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third day in a row.While airlines raced to get their schedules back on track, transportation secretary Sean Duffy said that things could return to normal by Monday (local time).The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is yet to identify the exact cause, even as the incident has renewed concerns about ageing technology and the need to upgrade the country's air traffic systems.The disruption continued to affect airlines across the country on Sunday. According to aviation data site FlightAware, more than 2,300 flights were cancelled and around 7,700 delayed.Saturday was even worse, with airlines cancelling more than 6,400 flights and reporting over 8,000 delays, according to Reuters.JetBlue saw the highest cancellations on Sunday, with 28% of its flights affected. American Airlines cancelled 17% of its flights, while United Airlines, Southwest and Delta reported cancellations of 3% to 5%.Speaking on ABC, Duffy said that flights would come "back to normal" on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday. He also stressed that keeping passengers safe remained the FAA's priority.One router, a chain of problems: What went wrongThe trouble started with maintenance work involving routers used by the FAA. According to officials, the installation of at least one new router by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility led to a huge flow of data at other air traffic control centres, affecting their communication systems.Duffy said the replacement of a router at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas. The Amarillo router began broadcasting, causing other routers at air traffic control centres across the country to become overloaded.The FAA said on Sunday that it had disabled the "functionality of the originating routers". It also took the same step for around 60 similar routers used in the air traffic control system.However, the exact reason behind the failure remains unclear. Duffy said the maintenance work had been carried out thousands of times in the past without any problems.The worker who installed the router was not suspected of deliberately causing the disruption.The worker was "a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran — so we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install," Duffy said. "But we don't actually have the root cause."Duffy also said the routers that experienced problems were bought in 2001 and had become outdated by 2006.FAA still has no clear answerThe technical failure led the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop on Friday, bringing nearly all departing flights to a halt for almost five hours.It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks on the United States.Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or any other deliberate attempt to disrupt the system. However, the FAA is still trying to establish what caused the failure.The incident has once again highlighted the challenges facing the US air traffic control system. It has been struggling with ageing technology, equipment and communication problems, along with a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.The flight disruptions have added urgency to the debate over modernising the country's air traffic control system.Duffy has called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure, raising his earlier demand of $30 billion. This is in addition to the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year.US President Donald Trump also called for more funding on Sunday, making his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions."We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," Trump wrote on social media. "Congress must approve."But the demand for more money has not gone unchallenged. US Representatives Rick Larsen and André Carson, the top Democrats on the House of Representatives Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and its aviation subcommittee, respectively, questioned why additional funds were needed.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Oil prices fall as surplus fears return after a nine-month dry spell in the market
articles.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday as concerns over a potential supply surplus weighed on the market, with shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovering to
articles.body: Oil prices fell on Monday as concerns over a potential supply surplus weighed on the market, with shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovering to nearly pre-war levels after months of disruption. The US has also eased restrictions on transporting fuel between its ports, adding to expectations of higher supply.WTI crude futures were trading at $88.35, down 21 cents or 0.24%, while Brent crude futures stood at $95.40, lower by 44 cents or 0.46%.The market is increasingly factoring in the possibility that available supplies could exceed demand in the coming months. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday that the global oil market is expected to move into a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, reversing its earlier forecast of a supply deficit.According to the agency, average oil supply during the quarter could reach 105 million barrels per day, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million barrels per day. The recovery in Middle East exports is expected to outpace growth in global demand, even as attacks on shipping continue."For the first time since the US-Iran conflict began, traders are actively contemplating the possibility of excess supply rather than persistent tightness. That shift in narrative is clearly dampening the tone," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.The IEA also said 71 million barrels from the record release of emergency oil reserves pledged by its members in March would be made available by the end of February. This includes 15 million barrels of diesel intended to ease tightness in the market.The downward movement in prices comes after both major benchmarks had already recorded steep weekly losses. Oil settled lower on Friday as traders assessed signs of reduced geopolitical risks from the US-Israeli war against Iran, now in its ninth month. WTI and Brent had shed 16% and 13%, respectively, over the previous week.Another factor weighing on crude prices is the US decision to extend the suspension of restrictions under the Jones Act for another 90 days.US President Donald Trump extended the waiver, a White House official said on Friday. The law normally requires cargo moved between US ports to be carried by US-flagged vessels. Its suspension allows foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and fuels, including petrol and diesel, between domestic ports, expanding the pool of available tankers.However, the easing of supply concerns does not mean lower shipping costs. Waterer said that elevated freight rates were continuing to support oil prices.The cost of transporting crude remains high because tankers face risks while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Vessel availability has also been affected by ships being tied up in transporting oil through the waterway, where cargoes are transferred to other vessels for onward delivery to refineries.The risks to shipping were highlighted again on Sunday night, when Iran's navy said an oil tanker had caught fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian government bonds could face fresh pressure at the start of the week, with rising US Treasury yields and a spike in domestic retail inflation weighing on market sentiment. The sharp selloff in US government debt last week pushed its 10-year yield up nearly 30 basis points, as investors factored in the possibility of a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike.The yield on India's benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond is likely to trade between 7.29% and 7.35% on Monday, a private-bank trader told Reuters. The bond had settled at 7.3079% on Friday.The US 10-year treasury yield closed Friday at around 5.15%, marking a 29-basis-point increase over the week. This was its steepest weekly rise in seven months and came amid growing concerns that the Federal Reserve could announce a larger-than-usual rate hike.The upward movement in US yields followed stronger-than-expected consumer price data for October and hawkish comments from some Federal Reserve members. These developments prompted markets to raise their bets on a bigger rate increase at the Fed's December 9 meeting.Traders are now assigning a 6% probability to a 50-basis-point hike on December 9, according to the CME FedWatch tool.The rise in US yields has also affected domestic bond market sentiment. India's 10-year benchmark yield increased 12 basis points last week, reversing half of the decline recorded during the first week of November."Rising US yields are likely to weigh on sentiment in the local market, especially after the sharp move witnessed in the previous week. Traders will be cautious, and the 10-year bond yield could test fresh highs," the trader said.The domestic inflation numbers have added another concern for the bond market. India's retail inflation accelerated to 6.09% in October, compared with 5.54% in September, crossing the upper tolerance band of the Reserve Bank of India's inflation target.According to STCI Primary Dealer, the latest inflation reading signals upward risks to food inflation, although fuel prices remain controlled for now.The increase in retail inflation has also strengthened expectations of another interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India in early December.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge
articles.summary: A proposed class action says Intel hid the impact of slowing sales, inflating its shares.
articles.body:
Shareholders have sued US chip giant Intel, accusing it of hiding the severity of a slump in personal computer (PC) sales, which they say led to a nearly 29% one-day collapse in the firm's stock.

A proposed class action lawsuit in San Jose, California said Intel was too late to alert shareholders about how slowing sales could impact its earnings, allegedly artificially inflating its stock price.

Intel shares plunged on 30 October, erasing tens of billions of dollars off its market value the day after it forecasted disappointing revenue in its coming earnings report.

The BBC has contacted Intel for comment.

The lawsuit, filed by legal firm Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd on behalf of owners of Intel common shares between 23 July and 29 October this year, was filed against the chipmaker, its chief executive Tan Lip-Bu and other company leaders.

Intel has been accused of making "materially false and/or misleading" statements that failed to disclose the slowdown in PC sales and the impact of its data centre projects, the complaint said.

In October, the firm announced that its computer hardware sales had dropped sharply in the three months that ended in September. That report undermined earlier suggestions from Intel that demand had been improving, sending Intel shares plunging, according to the lawsuit.

The lawsuit said the "depressed demand for PC sales" caused "a dramatic slowdown" in quarterly earnings – a drop of 9%, or about $800m, to $8.1bn.

Intel has poured huge investments into manufacturing to meet the enormous demand for AI computing power.

As more semiconductors are channelled towards data centres, chips for PCs and other electronics have become more expensive.

Intel boss Tan had told analysts that the industry was facing an "unprecedented memory crunch", resulting in a shortage of chip supplies for PCs.

"We need to address these challenges with urgency," Tan said in October.

Intel shares have fallen sharply in the past month by 37.5%, though the stock is still up by 51% overall this year.

articles.title: Intel sued by shareholders after stock plunges 29% in a single day, wipes out $140 billion
articles.summary: Intel has been hit with a shareholder lawsuit accusing the US chipmaker of concealing mounting problems in its personal computer business, weeks before a
articles.body: Intel has been hit with a shareholder lawsuit accusing the US chipmaker of concealing mounting problems in its personal computer business, weeks before a disappointing financial forecast triggered a massive stock sell-off that wiped out nearly $140 billion in market value in a single day.The proposed class-action lawsuit, filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, on Friday, alleges that Intel misled investors by failing to disclose the extent to which slowing PC sales and an inventory glut were weighing on its business. The company's shares plunged 28.6% on October 30, marking their steepest single-day decline in decades and one of the biggest blows to its market valuation.The lawsuit has been brought by shareholders led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, a Michigan pension fund. Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and chief financial officer David Zinsner have also been named as defendants. The plaintiffs are seeking unspecified damages on behalf of investors who purchased Intel shares between July 23 and October 29.Why shareholders have sued IntelAccording to the complaint, Intel was too slow to inform investors about the impact of weakening PC demand and excess inventory on its revenue prospects. Shareholders argued that these problems outweighed the potential gains from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, including increased investment in data centres.The lawsuit also alleges that Intel had both the motive and opportunity to defraud investors when it raised capital in mid-August, halfway through what the plaintiffs described as a 'disastrous' third quarter. The company sold $23 billion worth of stock at $95 per share as it sought to expand its chip contract manufacturing business, a key component of Tan's strategy.The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations. The following day, its shares crashed 28.6%, erasing approximately $140 billion in market value.During an earnings call, Tan expressed disappointment over manufacturing supply shortages, an 'unprecedented memory crunch' and the resulting weakness in PC demand.'We need to address these challenges with urgency,' he told analysts.Intel has invested heavily in expanding its manufacturing capabilities, hoping to capitalise on growing demand for chips used in AI data centres. However, supply disruptions have made it difficult for the company to benefit fully from that demand. At the same time, rising memory prices have pushed up PC costs, further weighing on consumer demand.Intel shares remain under pressureThe October sell-off has continued to cast a shadow over Intel's stock, even as the broader market has shown signs of resilience. The company's shares came under renewed pressure during the following trading sessions, falling further amid a wider rout in semiconductor stocks.According to Yahoo Finance calculations, chip and memory companies collectively lost more than $400 billion in market value in a single session during the recent downturn. Intel was among the biggest casualties, with its market value falling sharply from its September levels.Intel shares closed at $59.66 on Friday, November 13. Despite the recent losses, the stock remains up 62% so far this year, although it has retreated significantly from its June 30 peak of $142.35.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Asian shares fall before Nvidia earnings, Anthropic IPO test tech rally
articles.summary: By Stella Qiu SYDNEY, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Asian shares fell on Monday after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, with the c...
articles.body:
SYDNEY, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Asian shares fell on Monday after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, with the chipmaker's earnings and Anthropic's IPO this week set to test whether the AI-fuelled bull market still has further to ‌run.

Later in the week, US President Donald Trump is set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines ‌of the APEC forum in Shenzhen to discuss nuclear arms reduction and the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Markets will also be alert for any hint of policymakers being receptive to the idea of an outsized 50-basis-point ​interest rate hike next month.

The minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting are due on Wednesday, while a parade of Fed speakers will be on the bill this week.

On Monday, S&P 500 futures slipped 0.2%, while Nasdaq futures lost 0.4%. European stock futures were up 0.2%.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 1.9%, dragged down by Taiwan's 4.7% tumble and South Korea's decline of 3%. Japan's Nikkei fell 1.7% as data showed the economy unexpectedly shrunk last quarter.

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., the main ‌maker of Nvidia's AI chips, fell 4%.

China's blue-chips skidded ⁠0.6% after data showed its economic activity lost some momentum in October. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index bucked the trend with a 0.8% rise.

Nvidia, the poster child of a four-year US bull market, saw its market value tumble to $3.9 trillion by Friday from about $5.8 ⁠trillion in early October, LSEG data showed, as investors rushed for the exits after Huang's departure.

Analysts expect earnings growth of 90% on revenue of $109 billion in Nvidia's fiscal third quarter when it unveils earnings on Tuesday, with all eyes on whether the new management will stick to the chipmaker's bullish outlook for next year.

"Options markets imply an earnings-day move of approximately +/-7%, yet ​I ​question whether the quarterly numbers will carry their usual significance," said Chris Weston, head of research ​at foreign exchange brokerage Pepperstone.

"Nvidia may well deliver another exceptional beat ‌and raise at tomorrow's earnings, but investors are increasingly trying to value a business in FY2028 and FY2029 potentially without the individual who architected its competitive advantage."

Trading in Claude chatbot creator Anthropic is scheduled to begin just two days later, setting up a real-time barometer for sentiment on the AI trade.

articles.title: Rupee rises 6 paise to 94.13 as crude oil prices ease, strong dollar limit gains
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rupee started the week on a stronger note, recovering 6 paise to trade at 94.13 against the US dollar in early deals on Monday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rupee started the week on a stronger note, recovering 6 paise to trade at 94.13 against the US dollar in early deals on Monday. Lower crude oil prices, gains in domestic equities and foreign investor purchases supported the currency, although a firm dollar and higher US Treasury yields restricted its gains.The currency opened at 94.22 at the interbank foreign exchange market and moved between 94.13 and 94.25 during early trade. This comes after rupee lost 7 paise in the previous session to settle at 94.19 against the dollar on Friday.Uncertainty surrounding US-Iran relations remained a factor for currency traders after Iran attacked a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday. The dollar also remained firm, with the dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of six currencies, rising 0.03 per cent to 103.44."We expect the rupee to trade with a negative bias on an overnight surge in the dollar and rising US Treasury yields. However, softening of crude oil prices and foreign inflows may support the rupee at lower levels. At the domestic markets, traders may take cues from the Empire State manufacturing index data from the US and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech," said Anuj Choudhary, research analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan told PTI.Oil prices provided some support to the rupee, with Brent crude, the global benchmark, trading 1.03 per cent lower at $94.85 per barrel in futures trade.Stock markets also began Monday's session in positive territory. The Sensex climbed 414.36 points to 82,010.15, while the Nifty advanced 102.10 points to 25,252.50 in early trade.Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth Rs 5,736.55 crore on Friday, exchange data showed.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India's latest data showed that the country's foreign exchange reserves had risen by $2.49 billion to $719.547 billion in the week ended November 6.This followed a decline of $2.691 billion in the previous week, when reserves fell to $717.056 billion.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Stocks decline in Asia as investor concerns over Nvidia fallout extend into another week
articles.summary: HONG KONG (AP) — Asian shares mostly declined Monday as investors’ worries over the future of the artificial intelligence trade extended into another week fo...
articles.body:
HONG KONG (AP) — Asian shares mostly declined Monday as investors' worries over the future of the artificial intelligence trade extended into another week following Nvidia's fallout .

U.S. equity futures were trading lower. Investors and traders are closely monitoring any signals on what is next for the global AI industry ahead of Nvidia's earnings report due Tuesday and Anthropic's massive stock market debut set for later this week.

Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO last week after his extramarital affair sparked U.S. national security concerns shook global markets. Huang has been one of the biggest advocates for AI and his downfall triggered questions over how the global AI boom could be impacted.

Those worries have spread to Asia, where AI hardware stocks are prominent on markets including in South Korea and Japan.

South Korea's benchmark Kospi index lost 2.8% to 5,142.84. Shares fell for memory chipmaker SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics , two of its most valuable companies. SK Hynix plummeted 5.5%, while Samsung Electronics gave up 3.2%.

Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.6% to 60,182.50 after official data Monday showed Japan's economy contracted in the latest quarter . Several of Japan's big AI stock names also traded lower. OpenAI investor SoftBank Group slipped 4.2%, while memory maker Kioxia Holdings dropped 5.5% and chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron dipped 5.2%.

Also a beneficiary of the global AI frenzy, Taiwan's Taiex sank 4.1%, with shares of its leading chipmaker TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., falling 3.4%.

There have been increasing concerns that the robust growth of the AI capital spending may slow, analysts have said, even before the Nvidia episode. For one, uncertainties surrounding developments of AI data centers in the U.S. were also growing following the U.S. midterm elections.

"The market was already worried about this risk before what happened at Nvidia," Zhiwei Zhang, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management said in a commentary Monday. "Now the risk has become even more serious."

Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rose 0.9% to 23,852.96. The Shanghai Composite index declined 0.4% to 3,621.46 following latest Chinese official economic data released Monday, including on retail sales and industrial production, that disappointed analysts.

Australia's S&P/ASX 200 edged down 0.2% to 9,064.30.

On Friday, Wall Street's benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.4% . The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged 0.1% higher, while the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.9%.

articles.title: AI agents could help banks generate nearly 3x returns over three years: McKinsey
articles.summary: Banks adopting artificial intelligence (AI) agents could recover their investments in around 10 months and generate returns of nearly three times the
articles.body: Banks adopting artificial intelligence (AI) agents could recover their investments in around 10 months and generate returns of nearly three times the initial outlay over three years, according to a report by McKinsey, which highlighted the technology's potential to reshape the banking sector.An analysis of 52 agentic AI use cases in banking found that the average investment payback period was approximately 10 months, while the estimated return on investment over three years stood at around 2.9 times, the report said.McKinsey said banks' competitive advantage would increasingly depend on how quickly they move beyond pilot projects and integrate AI into their operations, products and customer services.“The economics of banking may shift in quarters rather than years as AI changes what the work costs, how a bank and its customers interact, and how those customers choose,” the report said.AI productivity gains have yet to translate into significant earningsDespite the potential returns, McKinsey cautioned that improvements in employee productivity do not automatically lead to higher profits for banks.According to its 2026 State of AI survey, 80 per cent of respondents reported individual productivity gains from using AI. However, only 6 per cent said the technology accounted for a significant share of their earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT).The findings suggest a gap between the productivity benefits reported by employees and the financial gains being realised by organisations.Customer adoption of AI is also increasing. A survey of around 46,000 consumers across 13 countries found that 23 per cent were already using generative AI for banking-related tasks.Among those using AI for such activities, 74 per cent relied on platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, indicating the role of external AI tools in customers' banking-related interactions.Rising costs and security risks pose challengesThe report also flagged the financial and security risks associated with wider AI adoption. Spending on AI tokens, computing and operations could rise to as much as 20 per cent of labour costs, adding to the expenses banks would need to manage while deploying the technology.It also cited around USD 900 million in reported losses from AI-enabled crime recorded by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in 2025.McKinsey said banks would need to build what it described as institutional intelligence by bringing together reliable data, customer information, internal policies and the experience of senior employees.Data readiness remains a significant hurdle. As many as 48 per cent of banking executives surveyed identified it as their biggest obstacle to adopting AI.The report said banks would also need to establish clear permissions, continuous monitoring and human oversight to ensure AI agents operate safely.It added that institutions would be better positioned to capture the benefits of the technology if they redesigned entire business processes rather than simply automating individual tasks.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Debt, dues and deja vu: How poor nations end up paying more than they borrow
articles.summary: The debt burden on low and middle-income countries continues to rise, with repayments becoming more expensive and fresh loans costing more.
articles.body: The debt burden on low and middle-income countries continues to rise, with repayments becoming more expensive and fresh loans costing more. Their external debt reached a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, as countries paid more towards existing loans than they received in new funding. Borrowing costs also hit their highest levels in decades for some of the poorest economies, according to a World Bank report.The World Bank's International Debt Report 2026 said external debt increased 5.5 per cent from $8.9 trillion in 2024. This was the biggest annual rise since 2021. The increase was driven by higher borrowing, a recovery in lending from private lenders and a weaker US dollar, which raised the reported value of debt.Countries pay more than they receiveThe growing debt has increased the amount countries need to spend on repayments. In 2025, low- and middle-income countries spent $1.4 trillion on servicing their debt, which includes both principal and interest payments. This was 1.9 per cent more than in 2024 and the fifth consecutive annual increase.The amount paid towards debt was also much higher than the fresh funding received. Between 2022 and 2025, these countries paid around $436.1 billion more in debt repayments than they received in new financing. Payments to bondholders alone rose 13.7 per cent to $363.1 billion in 2025.Highlighting the pressure on poorer nations, the World Bank said, “The countries that can least afford it are paying the most to borrow.”Poorest countries face highest borrowing costsCountries eligible for funding from the International Development Association (IDA) faced particularly high borrowing costs. They paid an average interest rate of 8.2 per cent on new loans in 2025, the highest level since the late 1980s.Borrowing money from bondholders was even more expensive, with interest rates averaging 9.4 per cent during the year.However, the trend was different for countries borrowing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Their average interest rate fell to 5.5 per cent in 2025, compared with 5.8 per cent in 2024.Private lending and bond sales pick upLending by private creditors to developing economies also increased in 2025. The debt owed by low- and middle-income countries to private lenders rose 5.2 per cent to $5 trillion.Governments also raised more money through bond sales. Public-sector bond issuances jumped 34.6 per cent to $250.6 billion, the highest level since 2021, the report said.This activity has continued in 2026.Preliminary figures for January to August show that countries continued to issue bonds despite high borrowing costs. Several countries had already issued more bonds in the first eight months of 2026 than they had during the whole of 2025.The World Bank warned that rising debt repayments and high funding needs are leaving governments with less money to manage their finances. This is also increasing the risks linked to rising debt and the need to refinance existing loans.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Did Nvidia row push for a united anti-China stance? US, India sign accord to protect AI suppy chain: Report
articles.summary: India has joined the United States and several other countries in signing the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity,
articles.body: India has joined the United States and several other countries in signing the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, an agreement aimed at protecting critical technologies and artificial intelligence supply chains amid growing competition with China.US under-secretary of state for economic affairs Jacob Helberg said India, South Korea, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates had signed the declaration, according to a Financial Times report. Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission were expected to sign it the following week.Explaining the need for cooperation, Helberg told the Financial Times that AI supply chains span several countries, making their security a shared concern. “The know how to design a chip, the machine that makes it and the port that ships it can all be in different countries,” he said.“What makes the San Francisco Declaration historic is that Pax Silica partners have agreed to treat the security of those technologies and the infrastructure behind them as a shared responsibility,” Helberg added.The declaration, signed by the US and partners including Japan, Australia, Israel and the United Kingdom, seeks to establish a joint list of critical technologies and supply chains that underpin AI and require greater protection. These include semiconductors, critical minerals, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing.What is Pax Silica?The declaration is part of Pax Silica, a US-led initiative launched in December 2025 by Helberg. It is the US state department's flagship effort to strengthen cooperation among partner countries on AI-related supply chains, including critical minerals, energy inputs, semiconductor manufacturing and AI infrastructure.The initiative has expanded its membership through the 2026 summit, with Argentina, Chile, Costa Rica, El Salvador, the European Union, Germany, Greece, Kazakhstan, the Netherlands and Panama among the latest additions to the Pax Silica Declaration. The number of signatories has risen to 24, including India, Australia, Finland, Israel, Japan, Norway, Qatar, South Korea, Singapore, Sweden, the Philippines, the UAE and the UK.India-US cooperation on critical technologiesThe latest development comes amid expanding cooperation between India and the US on critical technologies and trusted infrastructure.Earlier this month, foreign ministers of the Quad grouping - India, the US, Japan and Australia - announced plans to provide more than $85 million in technical and financial assistance to expand access to trusted AI infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific.The announcement followed a meeting of the four countries' foreign ministers on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Summit in Georgia. US secretary of state Marco Rubio, external affairs minister S Jaishankar, Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian foreign minister Penny Wong attended the meeting.Washington also announced a separate $10 million allocation to support critical minerals recycling initiatives in India and ASEAN member states.The declaration comes ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen this week.The development comes at a time when concerns are mounting over the sustainability of the AI spending boom, particularly the massive investments being made by technology companies in Nvidia's chips and data centre infrastructure. Questions over whether these investments will generate adequate returns have weighed on investor sentiment, while the reported leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit at Nvidia has added to concerns about the outlook for the AI sector. As one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, Nvidia's performance and leadership remain closely watched for signals on the pace of future AI spending.Money habits form by age 7.
